title: Race condition between defer and decompose in step 6c/6d — item briefly open before blocked
description: When an item exceeds max gate rejections, step 6c calls _defer() which sets status to open and removes assignment. Step 6d then calls _maybe_decompose() which invokes an AI agent (up to 120s) and, on success, sets the item to blocked. Between defer and decompose completion, the item is open and unassigned — another agent could claim it from the ready queue before decomposition finishes and blocks it. Fix: either (1) set a transient status like decomposing before calling defer, (2) defer AFTER decomposition completes, or (3) hold a claim on the item during decomposition. The decomposition agent takes up to 120 seconds (_DECOMPOSITION_TIMEOUT), which is a significant window for re-claiming.
close_reason: Fixed: Reordered defer/decompose so decomposition runs FIRST while item is still assigned. Branch task/PokePoke-01hrs pushed with all quality gates passed. Significant branch divergence (176 commits) requires manual PR merge.

title: ObjectDisposedException on exit when evaluate_js called after WebView2 disposed
description:
On exit, pywebview throws ObjectDisposedException when evaluate_js is invoked after the WebView2 window has already been disposed:

  File edgechromium.py line 146, in evaluate_js
    self.webview.Invoke(...)
  System.ObjectDisposedException: Cannot access a disposed object.
  Object name: 'WebView2'

This happens because the orchestrator continues pushing UI updates (e.g. agent status, beads item closure) after the window teardown has begun. Fix: guard evaluate_js calls with a disposed/alive check, or stop pushing UI updates once the window is closing.
close_reason: Fixed by architecture - desktop_ui.py no longer uses evaluate_js. Uses direct in-process method calls via pywebview.api polling pattern. Shutdown sets _is_running=False preventing further calls.

title: Add desktop app build verification to pre-commit hooks
description: Add a pre-commit check that verifies the desktop app builds successfully (vite build) when desktop files are staged. Currently check-build.ps1 only validates Python syntax. The check should: (1) Detect staged desktop/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,css,html} files. (2) Skip if none are staged. (3) Run 'npm run build' in the desktop/ directory (which runs tsc -b && vite build). (4) Fail the commit if the build fails. This catches import errors, missing modules, and Vite config issues that tsc alone might miss. Can potentially be combined with the type-check into a single build step since 'npm run build' already includes tsc -b.
notes: Added desktop build verification to check-build pre-commit hook

title: Bundle Python app with PyInstaller
description: Set up PyInstaller (or cx_Freeze) to bundle the pokepoke Python package, all dependencies, and the Python runtime into a standalone executable. Create a PyInstaller .spec file with proper hidden imports, data files (prompts, config templates), and exclusions. Output should be a single-folder distribution that can run without a system Python installation. Must include pywebview and its WebView2 dependency.

title: Reduce per-agent timeout from 2 hours to 30-45 minutes
description: The default timeout_hours=2.0 in workflow.py process_work_item is far too generous. In the 20260318_172321 run, successful agents (7vqi, vf71, 5mal) all completed in 5-15 minutes. Hung agents consumed slots for 15-20+ minutes before any timeout mechanism could intervene. A 30-45 minute ceiling would recover slots from truly hung agents much faster while still giving complex tasks enough time. This is complementary to startup timeout (PokePoke-bg7f) and inactivity watchdog (PokePoke-qjo7) which handle specific hang patterns.
notes: Reduced default timeout_hours from 2.0 to 0.5 (30 minutes).

title: Pre-flight health checks and self-repair before work submission
description: In run 20260224_171341, 11 items were submitted to a broken environment after maintenance left stale locks and dirty repo state. All failed silently with 0 agent requests. A circuit breaker would only delay retries against the same broken state. Instead, implement health-gated work submission: (1) Before each work batch, run pre-flight checks: verify git status is clean, worktrees are creatable, required locks are available, disk space is sufficient. (2) If pre-flight fails, attempt automatic self-repair: clear stale locks (verify holder PID is dead), reset dirty git state, prune orphan worktrees. (3) If self-repair fails, log a detailed diagnostic and shut down gracefully rather than submitting doomed work. (4) Classify errors as environmental (stop all work) vs item-specific (skip item, continue). This replaces PokePoke-sjm6 which was framed as a circuit breaker.
close_reason: Closed

title: Agent SDK sessions silently die without recording failure
description:
In run 20260309_141908_18b81e96, 5 of 8 agents silently stopped producing output mid-work with no error, no completion status, and no orchestrator log entry recording their death. The orchestrator kept running (showed 'active=8' in poll logs) but the agents were already dead.

Evidence from the run:
- worker-7 (j8r5): Last log at 14:27:57, was mid-edit on config.py. No error recorded.
- worker-1 (0gy0): Last log at 14:33:19. No error recorded.
- worker-3 (un8k): Last log at 14:36:25. No error recorded.
- worker-4 (ig7o): Last log at 14:37:00. No error recorded.
- worker-8 (aumh): Last log at 14:58:40, was mid-test-run. No error recorded.
- Only 3 agents (workers 2, 5, 6) completed successfully.
- Orchestrator log shows only 2 'Completed work item' entries and stops at 14:55:46.
- No timeout, drain, orphan, or circuit breaker messages in orchestrator log.
- A zombie python process (PID 17500) remained running but produced no output.

The orchestrator poll loop showed 'active=8 max=8 slots=0' until 14:47, meaning it believed all 8 agents were running when at least 4 had already silently died ~20 minutes earlier.

Impact:
1. UI shows agent cards stuck at last activity with no indication the agent died
2. Work items remain assigned to dead agents (in_progress status never cleared)
3. Orchestrator wastes slots on dead agents instead of reclaiming them for new work
4. No error telemetry - impossible to diagnose root cause without manual log analysis
5. User sees agents 'working' in the UI for an hour when they actually died silently

Needed:
- SDK session health monitoring (heartbeat/ping) to detect dead sessions
- Timeout on SDK sessions that produce no tool calls for N minutes
- Record explicit failure when an agent session ends without completion
- Clear agent status in UI when session death is detected
- Unassign work items from dead agents so they can be reclaimed
close_reason: Added SDK session inactivity detection. _await_completion now monitors last_event_time and aborts sessions that produce no SDK events for session_inactivity_timeout seconds (default 600s). Dead sessions return explicit failure, freeing orchestrator slots and triggering work item unassignment.

title: Cleanup agent output not written to item log files
description: When the cleanup agent is invoked (e.g. from worktree_merge_handler pre-merge readiness check), its Copilot CLI output is not captured to any log file. The work item log only contains the main work agent output. The cleanup agent runs via _run_agent_with_ui which uses terminal_ui.ui.agent_output_for() for the desktop UI but no ItemLogger is created or passed. This makes debugging cleanup failures impossible from logs alone - you can only see what happened from the desktop UI screenshot. The cleanup agent should either get its own log file (e.g. items/<item_id>-cleanup_<agent>.log) or its output should be appended to the parent item log.
close_reason: Fixed: item_logger now threaded through cleanup agent invocations

title: Confusing UI for gate agent retry cycle
description:
The terminal UI for gate-agent-driven retries is hard to follow. Looking at PokePoke-bajj (rainbow_boa-worker-2) as an example:

1. Version numbering is backwards/unclear - the cards show v1, v2, v3 but the chronological order in the UI makes it hard to tell which attempt is which. The gate agent cards (v1 Gate Agent, v2 Gate Agent) interleave with work agent cards (v2, v3) in a confusing way.

2. The GATE FAILED badge appears on what looks like a completed card with 'Added comment', 'Restarting Work Agent with feedback', making it unclear whether the item ultimately succeeded or failed.

3. When the gate agent rejects work and the work agent retries, there is no clear visual separation between attempts. The user sees a stream of cards (work v1 -> gate v2 rejection -> work v2 retry -> gate v1 passed) with no obvious timeline or grouping.

4. The gate agent rejection reason is truncated and requires expanding to understand what happened, but even expanded it is mixed in with other workers' output.

5. Suggestion: Group retry attempts visually (e.g. 'Attempt 1', 'Attempt 2'), show a clear retry arrow/indicator between attempts, and make the final outcome (pass/fail) prominent at the top of the card group rather than buried in the middle of the timeline.

title: sdk_await.py treats crashed CLI process as successful when no tool calls are pending
description:
Logic bug in sdk_await.py found by code review agent during run 20260325_180125_5ed28bc6 (but not filed by the agent).

The completion check uses: has_done_work and (no_pending or process_exited_ok)

When the CLI crashes (exit code 1) but there are no pending tool calls (no_pending=True), the expression evaluates to True because True or False = True. This means a crashed process is incorrectly treated as successful completion.

Python evaluation: True and (True or False) = True

Impact: Work items whose CLI process crashed may be marked as successfully completed, bypassing retry logic and potentially merging incomplete/broken work.

Remediation: The logic should be: has_done_work and no_pending and process_exited_ok (use AND instead of OR)

Affected code: src/pokepoke/models/sdk_await.py (completion check logic)
close_reason: Completed by PokePoke orchestrator (agent did not close)

title: Duplicate merge logic in worktree_finalization.py and worktree_merge_handler.py causes behavioral divergence
description:
## Summary

worktree_finalization.py (merge_worktree_to_dev, lines 92-187) and worktree_merge_handler.py (_handle_worktree_merge_inner, lines 53-174) contain nearly identical merge-attempt-cleanup-retry logic that has already diverged in behavior.

## Divergences Found

1. **Conflict details**: worktree_finalization.py builds a detailed conflict_details string with file list for the cleanup agent prompt; worktree_merge_handler.py does not, giving the cleanup agent less context
2. **Conflicted file display**: finalization shows up to 10 files, merge_handler shows up to 5
3. **Manifest tracking**: merge_handler tracks failed worktrees via add_uncleaned_worktree(); finalization does NOT, leaving orphaned worktrees untracked
4. **Repo root**: finalization uses Path.cwd() (fragile, depends on caller cwd); merge_handler takes repo_root as parameter (correct)
5. **Import style**: finalization uses late imports inside function body; merge_handler uses imports at function top
6. **Return type**: finalization returns bool; merge_handler returns tuple[bool, bool] (merge_success, worktree_cleaned)

## Impact

- **Orphaned worktrees**: Items processed through worktree_finalization.py that fail to merge are NOT tracked in the manifest, so cleanup never finds them. Disk usage grows silently.
- **Maintenance burden**: Any bug fix or behavior change must be manually mirrored in both files. The divergences above show this is already failing.
- **Inconsistent cleanup agent prompts**: One path gives the cleanup agent detailed conflict info, the other doesn't, leading to different success rates depending on which code path runs.

## Fix

Extract the shared merge-attempt-cleanup-retry pattern into a single function (e.g., in a new merge_logic.py or consolidate into worktree_merge_handler.py). Both call sites should delegate to the shared implementation. The merge_handler version is closer to correct (uses parameters, tracks manifest, returns cleanup status).
close_reason: Consolidated duplicate merge logic into perform_worktree_merge

title: MCP Tool Issue: check_node_health - overall_status HEALTHY despite component failures
description:
**Problem:**
check_node_health returns overall_status='HEALTHY' even when individual components report failures. Specifically, in testing with node 780bae64-734f-01a5-4c18-000931fbfce7:

- heartbeat.wireserver_status: HEALTHY
- heartbeat.imds_status: HEALTHY  
- service_requests.imds_status: 'UNHEALTHY - Zero successful requests'
- node_state.error: 'Request is invalid... BadRequest_CalloutBlockedByPolicy'

Yet overall_status = 'HEALTHY'

**Impact:**
An AI agent checking overall_status during incident investigation will be told the node is HEALTHY when it clearly has issues. This could cause the agent to:
- Skip further diagnosis ('node is healthy, problem must be elsewhere')
- Report misleading status to human operators
- Miss the actual root cause

The IMDS service requests being at zero while heartbeat shows healthy is itself a contradictory signal. Is IMDS healthy or unhealthy? The node_state error from blocked cluster access also indicates a real issue that's being ignored in the overall assessment.

**Expected:** overall_status should reflect the WORST component status or at least 'DEGRADED' when any component shows unhealthy/error.
**Actual:** overall_status='HEALTHY' with components showing UNHEALTHY and errors.
close_reason: MCP server issue - not in PokePoke scope, filed by beta test agent accidentally

title: execute_merge_sequence does not restore original branch on failure
description: git_operations.py execute_merge_sequence() does git checkout target_branch then git pull --rebase then git merge. If the merge fails, the caller is left on target_branch - there is no try/finally to restore the original branch. Combined with beads stash pop logic, a failure during merge leaves the repo dirty on the wrong branch. Subsequent operations that assume they are on their working branch will operate on target_branch instead, potentially corrupting it. The beads stash may also be silently lost if the process crashes between stash push and pop.
close_reason: Work merged into master - merge sequence improvements completed in prior commits

title: Code Review: beads stash recovery nukes working tree
description:
Problem:
restore_beads_stash (src/pokepoke/git_helpers.py, lines 61-66) runs `git checkout -- .` whenever `git stash pop --index` conflicts. That helper is invoked automatically after each orchestrator pull to restore .beads, so a conflict in .beads forcibly resets the ENTIRE working tree, wiping unrelated tracked edits and untracked files outside .beads.

Impact:
A routine stash conflict instantly destroys the developer's work and leaves the repo inconsistent, which is a high-severity data-loss bug. The helper should only intervene on .beads, not rewrite every file.

Suggested Fix:
Limit the cleanup to the .beads path (e.g., `git checkout -- .beads/` or restore via pathspec) and drop the repo-wide checkout. Alternatively, checkout only the stash paths you need and only drop the stash once recovery succeeds.

title: Thread-unsafe global _active_backend in beads_query.py causes race condition in multi-repo mode
description:
## Bug Description

The beads CLI backend selector (_active_backend in beads/beads_query.py:53) is a plain module-level global variable with NO thread-safety protection. set_active_backend() (line 68) writes it via 'global _active_backend', while _run_bd() (line 132) reads it without any lock. When multi_repo_aggregator.py:155 dispatches parallel ThreadPoolExecutor workers across multiple repos, concurrent calls to set_active_backend() and _run_bd() create a classic TOCTOU race condition — one repo's beads commands can silently execute against the wrong backend (bd vs br).

## Impact
- Silent data corruption: work items assigned/closed via wrong backend CLI
- Non-deterministic failures in multi-repo autonomous mode
- Extremely hard to reproduce or debug (timing-dependent)

## Root Cause
- beads_query.py:53 — _active_backend: CLIBackendConfig = BD_CONFIG (unprotected global)
- beads_query.py:68 — set_active_backend() mutates global without lock
- beads_query.py:132 — _run_bd() reads global without lock
- multi_repo_aggregator.py:155 — ThreadPoolExecutor spawns parallel workers that may each set different backends

## Recommended Fix
Replace global _active_backend with one of:
1. Thread-local storage (threading.local()) so each worker thread has its own backend
2. Pass backend config explicitly through the call chain (preferred — eliminates global state entirely)
3. At minimum, add a threading.Lock around set/get of _active_backend

Option 2 is the cleanest: add a 'backend' parameter to get_ready_work_items(), _run_bd(), and callers, threading it from the repo config. This aligns with the existing protocols.py BeadsClient pattern.

title: Move bd sync outside claim lock in assign_and_sync_item — wastes agent slot for up to 180s

The sync is best-effort visibility, not correctness-critical — the claim is already verified before sync runs. Move the bd sync call outside the lock scope so the agent slot is freed immediately after claim verification succeeds. Impact: in parallel mode, one hung bd sync blocks an agent semaphore slot for up to 3 minutes, reducing effective parallelism.

title: Orchestrator resubmits already-completed work items to new agents
description:
During run 20260325_180125_5ed28bc6, multiple items were assigned to agents despite the work already being done:

1. PokePoke-ab2w ('Extract SDKWatchdog'): Agent discovered sdk_watchdog.py already existed and sdk_helpers.py already had re-exports. A previous agent working on the parent epic PokePoke-t3gf had already completed the extraction. The agent wasted a full session discovering this.

2. PokePoke-zpd5 ('shutil.rmtree follows symlinks'): Agent found the fix was already implemented — _safe_rmtree() already uses os.walk(followlinks=False) with SymlinkFoundError and PathBoundaryError guards. The bug was already fixed but the item remained open.

Root cause: The orchestrator picks items from the ready queue based on beads status (open) but doesn't verify whether the actual code change has already been made. Items can be open in beads even though their acceptance criteria are already met.

Remediation options:
1. Add a pre-assignment check that runs a quick validation (e.g., grep for key acceptance criteria) before assigning to an agent
2. Close items automatically when their branch has been merged to master
3. Add a 'verify-still-needed' step in the agent's first action before starting work
4. Track which commits have been merged and cross-reference with item descriptions

Affected code:
- src/pokepoke/orchestration/workflow.py (work item assignment)
- src/pokepoke/beads/beads_management.py (ready queue filtering)

title: Decompose process_work_item() monolith and adopt RetryContext
description:
## Problem

`process_work_item()` in `orchestration/workflow.py` (lines 40-362) is a 323-line monolith with **11 levels of nesting** and an explicit `C901` complexity marker. It is the single most critical function in the codebase — every work item flows through it — yet it remains the least decomposed.

### Key structural issues:

1. **Gate retry loops (lines 253-352)** — Nested crash/timeout retry counters with manual state tracking across 3 nesting levels. This is exactly what `NestedRetryContext` in `retry_context.py` was designed to eliminate, but it is not used.

2. **Work agent loop (lines 136-226)** — Mixes timeout restart logic, feedback accumulation, session resumption, and stats extraction in a single while loop with deep nesting.

3. **Manual retry state fragmentation** — `timeout_restart_count`, `gate_crash_attempts`, `gate_timeout_attempts`, `resume_session_id`, `accumulated_feedback` are all tracked as bare local variables instead of using the purpose-built `RetryContext`/`NestedRetryContext` classes that already exist in `retry_context.py`.

### Why this matters:

- **Testability:** Individual phases (work loop, gate verification, finalization) cannot be tested in isolation without mocking the entire 323-line function. This directly blocks PokePoke-4pyu (test resilience).
- **Bug surface area:** 11 levels of nesting with interleaved retry/timeout/resume state makes reasoning about control flow error-prone.
- **Wasted infrastructure:** `RetryContext` (140 lines) and `NestedRetryContext` (37 lines) were purpose-built for this exact scenario but sit unused.

## Proposed Remediation

**Phase 1 — Extract loops into helpers:**
- `_run_work_agent_loop(item, worktree, config, retry_ctx) -> WorkLoopResult` — encapsulates lines 136-226
- `_run_gate_with_retries(item, worktree, config, nested_ctx) -> GateResult` — encapsulates lines 253-352

**Phase 2 — Adopt RetryContext:**
- Replace manual `timeout_restart_count` / `gate_crash_attempts` / `gate_timeout_attempts` with `RetryContext` and `NestedRetryContext`
- Use `retry_ctx.should_continue()`, `retry_ctx.record_retry()`, `retry_ctx.is_recurring_error()` instead of bare counter arithmetic

**Phase 3 — Reduce nesting:**
- After extraction, `process_work_item()` becomes a linear sequence: validate -> work loop -> cleanup -> gate -> finalize
- Target: <100 lines, max 3 levels of nesting

## Note
`workflow_helpers.py` already contains 12 extracted helpers (`_setup_worktree`, `_pre_loop_validate`, `_run_gate_check`, etc.) showing decomposition was started but not completed for the two most complex sections.

title: Shutdown watchdog os._exit(130) bypasses all cleanup, can corrupt merge state
description: In shutdown.py line 194, the watchdog thread calls os._exit(130) after the grace period (5s + 3s per agent). This is a hard process kill that: (1) Skips all finally blocks and context managers - any in-progress merge is left in a half-committed state with merge markers in the working tree, (2) Does not flush file handles - beads_item_stats_store and model_stats_store JSON files can be partially written and corrupted on next load, (3) Leaves file locks held (filelock-based coordination locks become stale), (4) Orphans child processes (git, copilot CLI) on Windows since os._exit does not propagate signals to the process group, (5) The merge queue shutdown thread (line 76-81) is a daemon thread that gets killed when the watchdog fires, so pending merges are silently dropped. With 3 agents running, the watchdog fires after just 14 seconds. Since merges have 60-120 second timeouts, a Ctrl+C during a merge almost guarantees the watchdog fires mid-merge. Fix should replace os._exit() with a cooperative shutdown that waits for the merge lock to be released before force-killing, and ensures stats store writes are atomic (write-to-temp + rename).
close_reason: Implemented: cooperative shutdown watchdog (no os._exit), reliable merge-queue shutdown, and atomic stats-store writes

title: Resume timed-out SDK sessions instead of starting fresh
description:
When a Copilot SDK session times out (per-item timeout), the orchestrator currently discards all context and starts a completely new session on retry. This loses all tool results, file reads, reasoning, and progress the agent had made.

The SDK supports session resumption via the session_id parameter and persistent session state in ~/.copilot/session-state/{session_id}/. The on_session_start hook distinguishes 'new' vs 'resume' vs 'startup' sources, confirming the SDK has built-in resume support.

Proposed approach:
1. Generate a stable session_id per work item (e.g. based on item ID + attempt number or just item ID for resume)
2. On timeout, reuse the same session_id when creating the next session
3. Use on_session_start hook to detect whether the session actually resumed (source='resume') vs started fresh
4. If resumed, send a shorter prompt with just the retry feedback rather than the full original prompt
5. If the SDK doesn't actually restore history via session_id reuse, fall back to get_messages() to capture history before timeout and inject a summary into the retry prompt

This would dramatically improve retry success rates since the agent wouldn't need to re-read files and re-discover the codebase on each attempt.
close_reason: Implemented in commit bf65001 on master - session resume with stable session_id, context injection, and 538 lines of test coverage

title: Memory circuit breaker resets on monitoring failure: fail-open under load
description:
## Summary

The memory circuit breaker in the parallel worker pool has a fail-open design flaw: when get_available_memory_mb() fails (returns 0), the circuit breaker resets its consecutive-low-polls counter to 0 instead of holding steady. A transient monitoring failure actively undoes accumulated pressure detection.

## Affected Code

parallel_worker_pool.py:295-310 -- update_memory_circuit_breaker():

    if available_mb > 0 and available_mb < memory_floor_mb:
        consecutive_low_polls += 1
    else:
        consecutive_low_polls = 0  # BUG: resets counter on failure

process_utils.py:141-143 -- get_available_memory_mb():

    except Exception as e:
        return 0  # Indistinguishable from non-Windows case

process_utils.py:146-151 -- is_memory_pressure():

    if available == 0:
        return False  # Assumes OK when unable to determine

## Impact

Under extreme system load (the exact scenario where protection matters most):

1. ctypes GlobalMemoryStatusEx call may fail under heavy memory pressure
2. get_available_memory_mb returns 0, indistinguishable from non-Windows
3. apply_memory_backpressure returns full slot count (no throttling)
4. update_memory_circuit_breaker RESETS consecutive_low_polls to 0, erasing accumulated evidence
5. More agents are spawned, further stressing the system -- positive feedback loop

The failure mode is exactly backwards: the circuit breaker disarms precisely when the system needs it most.

## Proposed Fix

Distinguish monitoring-unavailable from monitoring-confirms-OK:

    if available_mb > 0 and available_mb < memory_floor_mb:
        consecutive_low_polls += 1
    elif available_mb > 0:
        consecutive_low_polls = 0  # Confirmed above floor -- safe to reset
    # else: available_mb == 0 -- unknown state, preserve counter as-is

For is_memory_pressure() and is_memory_critical(), consider failing closed (return True) when monitoring fails on Windows, since the inability to check memory on a Windows system IS itself a signal of system distress.

title: Code Review: kill_process_tree on Unix only kills parent PID, orphans children
description: File: src/pokepoke/utils/process_utils.py, lines 274-306. The kill_process_tree() function docstring claims it kills the entire child tree, but the Unix code path only calls os.kill(pid, 9) which sends SIGKILL to the single PID. Unlike Windows taskkill /F /T, os.kill does NOT kill child processes. Children get reparented to init/PID 1 and continue running as orphans. Fix: Use os.killpg(os.getpgid(pid), signal.SIGKILL) to kill the process group, or iterate children via psutil (already a dependency) before killing the parent.

title: Code Review: repo-filtered model history truncates results
description:
Problem:
get_model_history in src/pokepoke/desktop_api_stats.py (lines 114-171) calls load_model_history_entries(limit=limit) and *then* filters entries by repo_name. When repo_name is provided, the first `limit` rows are usually a mix of repos, so filtering after the fact often returns far fewer results (even zero) despite older entries existing for that repo just past the limit. The UI therefore shows empty history for active repos once other repos fill the latest window.

Impact:
Per-repo trend charts and history inspectors silently truncate data and frequently show nothing for busy repos, making debugging impossible once more than ~limit entries exist globally.

Suggested Fix:
Apply the limit after filtering: continue reading until the filtered list reaches the limit or exhaust the file, or plumb repo_name into load_model_history_entries/model_stats_store so the backend filters before slicing.
notes: Already fixed in commit e25f126. load_model_history_entries filters by repo_name during reading and applies limit afterward. Regression tests exist.

title: desktop_api.py: inconsistent lock usage - 6 public methods mutate shared state without acquiring _lock
description:
## Problem

DesktopApi (desktop_api.py) has an RLock (self._lock) that is used by some methods (push_log, clear_logs, get_logs_since) but NOT used by 6 public state-mutation methods:

- push_work_item() (line 170)
- push_agent_name() (line 191)
- push_progress() (line 195)
- set_session_start_time() (line 178)
- set_session_end_time() (line 183)
- set_live_session_stats() (line 187)

These methods are called from agent worker threads (parallel mode) while get_state() reads all these fields from the UI polling thread without holding the lock. This creates a window where get_state() can observe logically inconsistent state (e.g., work_item from agent A but agent_name from agent B).

## Current Risk

Under CPython's GIL, individual attribute assignments are atomic, so this doesn't cause crashes today. However:
1. get_state() reads are not atomic across multiple fields - UI can show inconsistent combinations
2. Python 3.13+ introduces free-threading (PEP 703, no-GIL mode) which makes these real data races
3. The inconsistent lock pattern is confusing - developers can't tell which fields need protection

## Recommended Fix

1. Wrap all state-mutation methods in 'with self._lock:' blocks
2. Wrap get_state() field reads in 'with self._lock:' to ensure consistent snapshot
3. Consider a frozen snapshot pattern (similar to SessionStatsSnapshot in types.py) for the UI state

## Impact
- Reliability: Inconsistent UI state in parallel agent mode
- Forward compatibility: Will become a real data race with free-threaded Python
- Code quality: Inconsistent locking pattern confuses contributors
close_reason: Closed

title: Orchestrator must verify cleanup agent post-condition and retry on failure

title: pending_tool_calls counter double-incremented under two different locks — watchdog sees 2x actual value
description: sdk_event_handler.py _on_tool_start() increments pending_tool_calls TWICE per tool: once at line 160-161 under _pending_tool_calls_lock, and again at line 178 under _pending_tools_lock. _on_tool_complete() similarly decrements twice at lines 186-187 and 201 under the two different locks. This causes THREE problems: (1) The counter is always 2x the actual pending count, so the watchdog misjudges session health. (2) The two increments/decrements use DIFFERENT locks, creating a race window where the counter is at an intermediate value. (3) Asymmetric early returns cause permanent counter drift: _on_tool_start returns early (line 165) after one increment but before the second; _on_tool_complete returns early (line 191) after one decrement but before the second. Over a session with many tool calls, the drift accumulates and the counter becomes meaningless. The watchdog (sdk_watchdog.py) uses get_pending_tool_calls() (line 80-83) for idle detection and timeout decisions. An inflated/drifted counter can cause premature session abort or failure to detect a truly hung session. FIX: Remove the second increment at line 178 and second decrement at line 201. All counter modifications should go through _pending_tool_calls_lock only. The _pending_tools_lock should only guard the _pending_tools dict, not the counter.

title: merge_worktree reports failure after successful git push if post-push verification fails
description:
## Problem

In `worktrees.py` lines 153-163, after a successful `git push`, the merge verification check can fail and return `(False, [])`:

```python
subprocess.run(["git", "push"], check=True, ...)  # Push SUCCEEDS
print(f"Pushed {target_branch} to remote")

# Verification can fail even though push succeeded
if not is_worktree_merged(item_id, target_branch):
    print(f"Merge confirmation failed")
    return False, []  # Returns FAILURE despite successful push!
```

## Impact

- The merge is already pushed to remote, but the orchestrator treats it as a failure.
- The work item is NOT marked complete and will be re-processed.
- Re-processing creates duplicate merges or merge conflicts with the already-pushed work.
- The `is_worktree_merged` check uses `git branch --merged` which can have transient issues (e.g., refs not yet updated after push).

## Fix

After a successful push, treat verification failures as warnings rather than hard failures. Alternatively, use a more reliable check (verify the task branch HEAD is an ancestor of the target branch via `git merge-base --is-ancestor`).

```python
if not is_worktree_merged(item_id, target_branch):
    logger.warning(f"Post-push merge verification failed for {branch_name}, but push succeeded")
    # Don't return failure - the push already happened
```

## Files
- `src/pokepoke/worktrees.py` lines 153-163

The Copilot SDK powershell tool does NOT emit streaming events while a subprocess runs, so long commands like git commit (which triggers pre-commit hooks running tests/coverage/linting for 5-10 minutes) produce zero events. The inactivity detector sees 600s of silence and aborts the session. This causes every commit attempt to fail identically: tool.start at T+0, no events, abort at T+600s. Confirmed in run 20260310_123001_4e173fed where cobra-worker-3 failed all 3 retry attempts at exactly 600s after each commit call (12:42:35->12:52:53, 12:54:44->13:05:06, 13:08:54->13:19:38). Fix: in _await_completion(), skip the inactivity timeout when stats['pending_tool_calls'] > 0. The per-item hard deadline (2h) is sufficient protection against truly stuck sessions.

title: TOCTOU race in coordination.py stale-lock removal allows double lock acquisition or deadlock
description:
## Summary

The \cquire_lock()\ function in \src/pokepoke/worktrees/coordination.py\ has a classic **Time-Of-Check-Time-Of-Use (TOCTOU)** race condition in its stale-lock detection and removal logic. Two concurrent processes can both evaluate a lock as stale, both delete the lock file, and both acquire what they believe is an exclusive lock — violating mutual exclusion.

## Affected Code

**File**: \src/pokepoke/worktrees/coordination.py\, function \cquire_lock()\ (lines ~109-140)

## The Race

\\\
Process P1                              Process P2
─────────                               ─────────
lock_path.exists() → True
                                        lock_path.exists() → True
stat().st_mtime → age=950s (> stale)
                                        stat().st_mtime → age=950s (> stale)
_is_pid_alive(holder) → False
                                        _is_pid_alive(holder) → False
lock_path.unlink()  ← removes file
                                        lock_path.unlink()  ← already gone, no-op (missing_ok=True)
lock.acquire() → SUCCESS
                                        lock.acquire() → SUCCESS  ← BOTH hold 'exclusive' lock!
\\\

## Impact

- **Mutual exclusion violation**: Two processes/threads both believe they hold an exclusive lock on the same resource (e.g., beads_db_lock, worktree_setup lock)
- **Data corruption**: Concurrent worktree creation or beads DB writes that should be serialized
- **Deadlock (secondary)**: If one process deletes a lock file that another process is about to acquire, the waiting process may hang indefinitely depending on FileLock implementation

## Context

This is most likely to trigger during:
- Parallel agent startup (multiple workers acquiring worktree_setup lock)
- High-concurrency beads operations (multiple workers claiming items)
- Recovery after a crash (stale locks from dead PIDs)

## Recommended Fix

Use an **atomic check-and-acquire** pattern:
1. Attempt \lock.acquire(timeout=0)\ first (non-blocking)
2. Only if that fails AND the lock is stale (age > threshold, holder PID dead), then break the lock
3. Use a separate meta-lock (or filesystem atomic rename) to serialize the stale-detection logic itself
4. Alternative: use \FileLock.acquire(timeout=stale_timeout)\ and let the timeout handle staleness naturally, removing the manual stale detection entirely

## Related

- PokePoke-wz1z2: config cache thread safety (different subsystem)
- PokePoke-s8og5/z1i3t/aifvc: stale worktree reaper (runtime mitigation, not the root cause)

title: Add shared git-operations lock for main repo to prevent index.lock contention between poll loop and merge queue
description: CRITICAL: The poll loop's check_and_commit_main_repo (repo_check.py) runs git add/commit on the main repo on its own thread. The merge queue worker thread (merge_queue.py) also runs git checkout/merge/pull on the main repo. Both operate on the same .git/index file WITHOUT a shared lock. In run 20260401_114342_2df28468, this caused 'Unable to create index.lock: File exists' at 11:59:31. 5-whys: (1) index.lock exists because another git process is running. (2) Two independent systems both run git in main: poll loop and merge queue worker. (3) They use separate locks (merge-queue.lock vs none). (4) No shared git-operations mutex exists. Fix: create a shared reentrant lock for ALL git operations on the main repo. Both the poll loop auto-commit and the merge queue worker must acquire this lock before any git command in main.
close_reason: Added shared threading.RLock (main_repo_git_lock) in coordination.py. Both repo_check.py and merge_queue.py now acquire it before git write operations on the main repo, preventing index.lock contention.

title: Code Review: gate_agent_enabled flag ignored
description:
## Problem
`ProjectConfig.gate_agent_enabled` (src/pokepoke/config.py:185) is never referenced anywhere else in the repo. `process_work_item` (src/pokepoke/workflow.py, gate agent block around line 234) always calls `run_gate_agent(...)` after cleanup, so disabling the flag in pokepoke.config.yaml has no effect.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Set `gate_agent_enabled: false` in pokepoke.config.yaml (or via CLI arguments).
2. Start the orchestrator and process any work item until the work agent finishes successfully.
3. Observe that after cleanup the gate agent still launches (status cards + console output) even though the flag is false.

## Impact
Teams that need to temporarily bypass the gate agent (e.g., during emergencies or while debugging flaky gate prompts) cannot do so. Every item still incurs the gate run, which burns additional requests/time and blocks desired workflows.

## Suggested Fix
Wrap the gate agent block in `process_work_item` with a `if not config.gate_agent_enabled` check: log that gate verification is disabled, set `gate_success = True`, skip calling `run_gate_agent`, and break out of the retry loop. That will make the config option functional again.
notes: Fix already implemented: workflow.py line 237-240 checks config.gate_agent_enabled and skips gate agent when disabled. Tests exist in test_config.py and test_workflow.py.

title: Agents running but no output reaches desktop UI - gate agents show 0 lines and 'Waiting for output'
description:
## Problem
Active agents show 'Waiting for output...' and '0 lines' in the desktop UI despite being actively running (gate checks executing, tool calls happening). The orchestrator log confirms agents are processing items (PokePoke-nc4s gate agent running, attempt 1+), but the UI panel shows no streamed output.

## Observed Behavior
- Screenshot shows 3 active agents for PokePoke-nc4s (v1 work agent, v1 gate agent, v2 gate agent)
- Gate agent v2 shows 'Running' status with 'Waiting for output...' and '0 lines'
- Gate agent v1 shows 'Running gate check..' but no output lines
- Work agent v1 shows GATE FAILED but also 'Waiting for output..'
- Orchestrator log confirms agents are doing real work (tool calls, file reads happening)

## Expected Behavior
Agent output should stream to the desktop UI in real-time as the Copilot SDK produces it.

## Impact
Users cannot monitor agent progress. The UI appears frozen/stuck even though work is happening in the background. This makes it impossible to supervise autonomous operation.

## Likely Root Cause
The refactor that replaced ~400 print() calls with logger.info/warning/error (commit f01e73e6) may have broken the output pipeline that feeds the desktop UI. The desktop terminal_ui or DesktopUI may be listening on stdout/print rather than the logging framework.
close_reason: Fixed: added DesktopLogHandler to route logger output to desktop UI agent panels

title: Code Review: Template include recursion has no depth limit — circular includes will crash orchestrator
description:
**File:** src/pokepoke/prompts/prompts.py, _process_includes() (line 325-347)

**Problem:** The template include system ({{>template_name}}) recursively resolves includes with no depth limit or cycle detection. If template A includes {{>B}} and B includes {{>A}}, Python hits RecursionError (default stack depth ~1000), crashing the prompt building path.

**Impact:** Crash in invoke_copilot_sdk -> build_prompt_from_work_item -> load_and_render -> _process_includes. This is the core orchestration path. Any accidental circular reference in .pokepoke/prompts/ would bring down the worker.

**Current state:** No cycles exist in current templates (desktop-work, orchestrator-work, tests-work all include beads-item which has no includes). But the code is not defensive.

**Suggested fix:** Add a 'seen' set or max_depth parameter (e.g., 10) to _process_includes. On cycle/depth exceeded, log a warning and return the raw include tag unresolved.

title: Tech debt maintenance agent cannot run bd commands - shell tools excluded by deny_write

The agent then spirals for ~38 minutes trying write_powershell workarounds before hitting the 1800s watchdog timeout. Either: (1) give beads-only agents a narrower exclusion list that permits shell but blocks file writes, (2) route tech_debt through _run_main_repo_agent which has deny_write=False, or (3) make the agent prompt aware it lacks shell so it reports findings without attempting bd commands.

title: Gate agent failure should resume gate, not retry entire work agent
description:
**Issue**: When a gate agent (validation agent) fails or crashes, the system retries the entire work agent from the beginning instead of just resuming/retrying the gate agent.

**Expected Behavior**: 
- Work agent completes successfully with valid output
- Gate agent validates the work (may crash/fail)
- If gate agent fails: Resume and retry ONLY the gate agent with the same work output
- Do NOT re-run the work agent from the start

**Current Behavior**:
- Work agent completes successfully 
- Gate agent fails/crashes
- System retries the ENTIRE work agent from the beginning (wasted compute, repeated tool calls, etc.)

**Root Cause**: Likely in orchestration.workflow or gate validation logic - probably treats gate agent failure the same as work agent failure instead of distinguishing between:
1. Work agent needs retry (incomplete output, invalid state)
2. Gate agent needs retry (validation failed, process crashed, but work output is valid)

**Impact**:
- Inefficient resource usage (re-doing completed work)
- Repeated API calls and tool invocations 
- Higher costs and longer execution times
- Poor separation of concerns between work generation and validation

**Observed in**: Run 20260324_161815_6ddaa210 - multiple Copilot failures leading to full work agent retry instead of focused gate agent retry

**Fix Strategy**: 
1. Distinguish gate agent failures from work agent failures in workflow state
2. When gate agent fails: Mark work as 'validated_but_gate_failed' or similar
3. On retry: Skip work agent, go directly to gate agent with cached output
4. Only retry work agent if gate cannot recover (e.g., fundamental validation failure)

title: Post-mortem agent: auto-review run logs, file issues, and resume to fix before shutdown
description: Add a new agent type that runs when the orchestrator is about to shut down (circuit breaker triggered, out of ready items, or manual stop). Instead of immediately exiting, the orchestrator invokes a 'post-mortem agent' that: (1) ANALYZE: Reads the current run's orchestrator.log and item logs from .pokepoke/logs/{run_id}/, identifies failure patterns (tool timeouts, merge conflicts, gate rejections, recurring failures on specific items), and categorizes them; (2) FILE: Creates beads items for each distinct issue found — with root cause analysis, affected item IDs, frequency counts, and suggested fixes. Labels items appropriately. Deduplicates against existing open issues to avoid filing known problems; (3) PRIORITIZE: Sets priority based on impact (e.g., a pattern causing 50% of failures is P0, a one-off is P3); (4) RESUME: After filing, the orchestrator resumes processing with ONLY the newly-filed post-mortem items in scope (filter ready queue to just these IDs). This gives the system a chance to self-heal before fully shutting down; (5) SHUTDOWN: After one pass through the post-mortem items (success or failure), the orchestrator completes its normal shutdown sequence. CONFIGURATION: Add post_mortem_enabled (bool, default true), post_mortem_max_items (int, default 5), post_mortem_timeout_minutes (int, default 30) to pokepoke.config.json. The agent should use a read-only session for analysis (deny_write=True for the analysis phase) and a normal session for the fix phase. TRIGGER CONDITIONS: Circuit breaker (10 consecutive failures), empty ready queue with items still open, explicit --stop signal, or configurable idle timeout.

title: Code Review: parse_repos_cli breaks Windows paths
description:
Problem:
parse_repos_cli (src/pokepoke/repo_config_loader.py, lines 101-137) blindly calls entry.split(":") to separate the path from key=value options. On Windows the drive letter introduces a colon, so an argument such as `C:\src\repo:weight=5` is split into path `"C"`, option `"\\src\\repo"`, and `weight=5`. RepoConfig then points to `C`, validation fails, and multi-repo CLI cannot be used on Windows at all.

Impact:
Every Windows user (our primary deployment environment) gets invalid repo paths when supplying absolute paths with --repos, so the feature is broken before validation even runs.

Suggested Fix:
Detect drive-letter prefixes (e.g., use pathlib.PureWindowsPath) or split only on the first colon *after* the path segment. One simple approach is to split once on the first colon not followed by a slash/backslash by using partition or regex, leaving the drive letter intact before parsing weight/max_worker options.

title: Merge queue retries permanent conflicts indefinitely with no retry cap or blacklist
description:
## Problem

When a merge conflict is permanent (cannot be auto-resolved), the orchestrator enters an infinite retry loop:

1. Item enters merge queue, hits unresolvable conflict
2. `invoke_merge_conflict_cleanup_agent()` runs but cannot fix the conflict
3. Merge returns `False` (failed) — no retry count tracked
4. Next orchestration loop re-selects the same item (still 'ready' in beads)
5. Same conflict, same cleanup attempt, same failure — forever

## Key Code Locations

- `src/pokepoke/worktrees/worktree_merge_handler.py` lines 188-226: cleanup agent invoked with no retry limit
- `src/pokepoke/git/merge_queue.py` lines 217-278: `MergeStatus.CONFLICT` is defined but never set; result is always SUCCESS or FAILED
- No blacklist or max-retry-count prevents re-queueing the same failed item

## Impact

- **Blocks all downstream merges** if queue is serial
- **Wastes compute** invoking cleanup agent repeatedly on unresolvable conflicts
- **Strands the work item** in a limbo state (not failed in beads, not mergeable)

## Recommended Fix

1. Track per-item merge attempt count in `MergeRequest` or session state
2. After N failures (e.g., 3), mark item as `blocked` in beads with `human-required` label
3. Set `MergeStatus.CONFLICT` explicitly so callers can distinguish conflict from other failures
4. Add a blacklist/cooldown to prevent re-queueing recently-failed items within the same session

## Related

- `PokePoke-9t2s` covers merge sequence refactoring but not the retry-cap/blacklist gap

title: Add concurrency stress tests for parallel agent execution
description:
**Problem:** The parallel agent loop (--max-agents > 1) has extensive unit tests (7 test files, ~2000+ lines), but nearly all mock away the ThreadPoolExecutor. Only ONE test across all parallel test files creates a real ThreadPoolExecutor with actual concurrent work. There are ZERO tests for:
- Circuit breaker behavior under real concurrent failure cascades
- Race conditions on shared mutable state (SessionStats, failed_claim_ids, config cache) under thread contention
- Deadlock scenarios with semaphores + merge lock + shutdown coordination
- Memory backpressure throttling under actual concurrent agent load

**Why it matters:** The parallel module manages real shared state across threads — SessionStats (with lock), failed_claim_ids (set, no lock in sequential path), module-level config cache (no lock). These are production code paths that run when --max-agents > 1. Without concurrency stress tests, thread-safety bugs (data races, deadlocks, lost updates) will only surface in production under load.

**Specific gaps:**
1. tests/agents/test_parallel_agents.py: Uses real threading.Thread + barriers but only for 2-thread scenarios, never stresses shared state
2. tests/agents/test_parallel_support.py: Tests dispatch_items and circuit breaker with mocked executor only — mock.call_count assertions don't prove thread safety
3. tests/agents/test_parallel.py: Has best coverage but only 1 real ThreadPoolExecutor test (lines 989-1000) with a single worker
4. No tests exercise the full run_parallel_loop() with real concurrent process_work_item calls (even with mocked beads/copilot)

**Recommended approach:**
- Add stress tests with 4-8 real ThreadPoolExecutor workers processing mock work items concurrently
- Verify SessionStats integrity after concurrent updates (compare expected vs actual counts)
- Test circuit breaker trips correctly after N consecutive real (not mocked) failures across threads
- Test semaphore + merge lock interaction under contention (no deadlocks)
- Use threading.Barrier to force simultaneous access to shared state
- Run tests with TSAN-like iteration (repeat 50x) to surface intermittent races

title: SDK client shutdown can block agent thread indefinitely when copilot process hangs
description:
In copilot_sdk.py (lines 312-319), when the initial client.stop() times out after 10 seconds, the fallback calls client.stop() AGAIN without any timeout. If the copilot subprocess is truly stuck (e.g., waiting on I/O, deadlocked), this second call hangs indefinitely, blocking the agent thread forever.

**Impact:** Each hung agent permanently consumes a slot in the ThreadPoolExecutor. Over time, multiple stuck agents can exhaust all parallel slots, making the system unable to process new work items. This is a progressive degradation that's hard to detect since there are no errors logged.

**Root cause:** Line 315 calls await client.stop() without asyncio.wait_for() timeout wrapper.

**Fix:** Wrap the fallback stop in asyncio.wait_for() with a shorter timeout (e.g., 5s), and if that also fails, forcibly kill the copilot subprocess via its PID. Something like:
  try:
      await asyncio.wait_for(client.stop(), timeout=5.0)
  except TimeoutError:
      logger.warning('Force-killing copilot process after double timeout')
      # Kill subprocess by PID if accessible from client
      
**Affected file:** src/pokepoke/copilot_sdk.py lines 312-319

title: UnicodeDecodeError in subprocess _readerthread using cp1252 codec
description: subprocess.communicate() reader thread crashes with UnicodeDecodeError when reading process output that contains bytes not valid in cp1252 encoding (byte 0x9d at position 70016). This happens because Python on Windows defaults to the system locale codec (cp1252) for subprocess pipes instead of UTF-8. The crash occurs in threading._bootstrap_inner -> subprocess._readerthread -> fh.read() -> codecs.charmap_decode. This likely affects copilot CLI output or git command output that contains Unicode characters (emoji, special chars). Fix: ensure subprocess pipes use encoding='utf-8' and errors='replace' or errors='backslashreplace' to handle arbitrary byte sequences gracefully. Additionally, a follow-on error occurs: 'Failed to backfill beads item stats: the JSON object must be str, bytes or bytearray, not NoneType' - likely because the subprocess output was None/lost due to the reader thread crash.
notes: Fixed: Added encoding='utf-8' and errors='replace' to all subprocess.run() calls. Added None guard in backfill.

title: Silent exception suppression in parallel_support.py can leave work items permanently assigned
description:
**Problem:** parallel_support.py uses contextlib.suppress(Exception) around unassign_with_retry() calls in two critical error-recovery paths (lines 91 and 225). If unassignment fails silently, work items remain permanently assigned to the crashed/failed agent with zero diagnostic output — they become invisible stuck items that never return to the ready queue.

**Affected code:**

1. parallel_support.py:91 — Orphan future cleanup:
   with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
       unassign_with_retry(item.id)
   If this fails, the orphaned item stays assigned forever.

2. parallel_support.py:225 — Executor submission failure:
   with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
       unassign_with_retry(item.id)
   If this fails, the item stays assigned despite no agent working on it.

**Impact:** In continuous autonomous operation, stuck items accumulate silently. The operator has no way to know items are stuck unless they manually audit beads state. This undermines the self-healing design of the retry loop.

**Note:** Other contextlib.suppress(Exception) uses in the codebase are acceptable (best-effort prune, temp file cleanup, stats collection). These two are problematic because they suppress failures in a critical recovery path with operational consequences.

**Recommended fix:**
- Replace contextlib.suppress with try/except that logs at WARNING level with the item ID and exception
- Consider adding a stuck-item audit to the maintenance cycle that detects items assigned for > N minutes with no active agent
- Distinct from PokePoke-esub (logging standardization) which covers print-vs-logger; this is about error swallowing in critical paths
close_reason: Fixed: replaced contextlib.suppress(Exception) with try/except + WARNING logging in two critical unassign paths

title: Design safe DI architecture for worktree and git tests to replace autouse safety fixtures
description: The 7 autouse fixtures in conftest.py exist for good reason - without them, tests run real git operations against the host repo. Specifically: (1) _force_sequential_mode prevents unmocked parallel loop from calling check_and_commit_main_repo() which runs real 'git add --all' + 'git commit', silently destroying staged work. (2) _block_real_git_repair prevents preflight self-repair from running real 'git add -u' + 'git commit' against the host repo. (3) _mock_cleanup_lock_global prevents xdist workers from deadlocking on shared .pokepoke/locks/. These are safety-critical, not convenience. But they hide real behavior and make tests pass in a phantom environment. The fix is NOT to remove the safety fixtures - it's to make them unnecessary through proper DI. Design: (1) Create a GitClient Protocol (from PokePoke-od1h) where the real implementation calls subprocess and the test fake records calls without executing them. Tests inject FakeGitClient instead of needing _block_real_git_repair. (2) Create a LockManager Protocol where tests inject an in-memory lock implementation. Tests no longer need _mock_cleanup_lock_global or _isolate_lock_dir. (3) Make orchestrator/workflow accept these as parameters so _force_sequential_mode becomes unnecessary - the parallel path uses the same injected fakes. (4) Keep the safety fixtures as a BELT-AND-SUSPENDERS backstop even after DI is in place - they become defense-in-depth rather than the primary safety mechanism. (5) Worktree tests should use a FakeGitClient that simulates merge conflicts, branch states, and worktree operations without touching the real filesystem. This is blocked by PokePoke-od1h (Protocol interfaces).

title: Code Review: repo picker crashes on headless environments
description:
## Problem
pick_repo_directory() only catches ImportError around the tkinter UI setup (src/pokepoke/repo_picker.py lines 45-127). On headless servers/CI (no DISPLAY) tkinter imports fine but 	k.Tk() raises _tkinter.TclError: no display name and no  environment variable. Because the exception isn't caught, the frozen binary exits with a stack trace before falling back to the console prompt.

## Impact
The new repo picker makes the packaged CLI unusable anywhere without a GUI (SSH session, CI job, Windows Server Core). Users cannot select a repo or run agents even though the previous build worked in these environments.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Build the PyInstaller binary (pyinstaller packaging/pyinstaller/pokepoke.spec).
2. On a headless machine (or run with DISPLAY= on Linux/macOS), execute the binary with no --repo argument.
3. The process crashes immediately with _tkinter.TclError and never shows the fallback prompt.

## Suggested Fix
Catch 	k.TclError (and other runtime exceptions) around the tkinter code path and fall back to the existing console prompt the same way the ImportError branch does. Optionally detect headless environments before instantiating Tk to avoid throwing in the first place.

title: Parallel agents need merge sequencing to prevent merge conflict cascades
description: During run 20260220_133831_cd6a9414, 5 parallel agents all completed work on separate worktree branches and attempted to merge back to master around the same time. This caused: (1) worker-2 hit a delete/modify conflict on .pokepoke/beads_item_stats.json during merge because worker-3 had already untracked it, (2) worker-5 had to resolve worker-2's incomplete/pending merge on master before it could merge its own branch, (3) the orchestrator detected uncommitted changes on master at 13:50 (from merge residue) and launched a heavyweight cleanup agent. We need a merge queue or sequencing mechanism so that when multiple agents finish around the same time, their merges to master are serialized and each merge starts from a clean, up-to-date master. Options: (a) a merge queue that agents enqueue into when done, processed FIFO, (b) a lock-based approach where only one merge runs at a time, (c) rebase-before-merge with automatic conflict detection and retry. This should also coordinate with cleanup agents so they don't run concurrently with merges.

title: Code Review: parallel single-shot keeps processing entire queue
description:
## Summary
Commit dbd2a24 removed the nd not (not continuous and any_success) guard inside run_parallel_loop() when replenishing slots (src/pokepoke/parallel.py:266-278). In non-continuous mode we now continue to select new items every time a worker finishes, so a single-shot parallel run drains the entire ready queue instead of stopping after the first success. This regresses the documented CLI behavior where default runs handle one bead unless --continuous is supplied.

## Impact
Running python -m pokepoke.orchestrator --autonomous --max-agents N now processes every ready work item in one session. Teams expecting a single bead to be claimed end up with multiple beads assigned, multiple branches created/merged, and much longer unattended runs. Sequential mode still stops after one item, so behavior diverges depending on --max-agents.

## Repro
1. Queue 3+ ready beads.
2. Run python -m pokepoke.orchestrator --autonomous --max-agents 3 (no --continuous).
3. Observe via logs that as soon as the first agent completes successfully, the orchestrator immediately refills its slot and keeps going until the queue empties instead of exiting the session.

## Expected
Non-continuous parallel runs should stop launching new work once any agent succeeds, mirroring the sequential orchestrator. After existing futures drain the session should finalize.

## Suggested Fix
Restore a guard so the replenishment block is skipped once continuous is False and we have already reported a success (e.g., track a session-level has_success flag or reuse ny_success). Alternatively trigger should_stop_after_current() once a success is recorded so the loop drains and exits without claiming new beads.

title: assign_and_sync_item leaves items permanently stuck when post-update verification fails
description:
Problem: In beads_management.py:assign_and_sync_item(), if the bd update command succeeds (line 145) but the subsequent verification step fails (lines 149-162), the function returns False without unassigning the item. The item is now in 'in_progress' status with an agent assigned, but no worker thread will ever process it.

Root cause (lines 143-169):
1. _run_bd(['update', item_id, '--status', 'in_progress', '-a', agent_name]) succeeds -- item IS now assigned in beads
2. _run_bd(['show', item_id, '--json']) fails (JSON parse error, subprocess timeout, or beads CLI error) -- OR the assignee field doesn't match expectations
3. Function returns False at lines 152 or 162
4. Caller (dispatch_items in parallel_support.py:213-215) adds item to failed_claim_ids and moves on
5. Nobody calls unassign_item() or unassign_with_retry() -- the item is stuck

Why existing recovery doesn't catch this:
- retry_failed_unassigns() at startup only recovers items added to the manifest via _add_failed_unassign(), which only happens when unassign_with_retry() fails. Since unassign is never attempted, the item is never added to the manifest.
- WorkItemSession.cleanup_on_failure() is never reached because the worker thread is never started.
- The contextlib.suppress issue (PokePoke-3vky) is orthogonal -- that covers failed unassign attempts, not missing unassign calls.

Impact: In autonomous 24/7 operation, any transient beads CLI failure during verification causes items to become permanently stuck. The failed_claim_ids set prevents re-claiming within the current session, and no cross-session recovery exists for this path.

Recommended fix:
1. Add unassign_item(item_id) calls before the return False statements at lines 152 and 162 of beads_management.py
2. If unassign fails, call _add_failed_unassign(item_id) from beads_recovery so startup recovery can handle it
3. Consider returning a richer result (e.g., a named tuple with claimed and needs_unassign fields) so callers can distinguish between 'never assigned' vs 'assigned but verification failed'

Distinct from PokePoke-3vky: That ticket covers silent exception suppression around unassign_with_retry() calls. This ticket covers the missing unassign call entirely in the verification-failure path of assign_and_sync_item().
close_reason: Fixed: added _rollback_assignment() to unassign items when post-update verification fails, with fallback to failed-unassign manifest for startup recovery

title: Stream tool command stdout/stderr to UI and logs in real-time for output-based liveness
description: Stream subprocess stdout/stderr from powershell tool calls to both the item log and the desktop UI in real-time. Currently PokePoke is completely blind during tool execution — it only sees SDK events, not the actual subprocess output. With streaming: (1) We can see if pytest is progressing or stuck; (2) We can detect commands waiting for stdin input (a suspected cause of many hangs); (3) The UI shows live agent activity instead of silence; (4) If output stops for N minutes while no child processes are active, we know it's truly hung vs legitimately computing. Implementation: intercept the Copilot SDK's tool execution subprocess pipe, tee stdout/stderr to the item logger and desktop bridge. The SDK's _STREAMING_ATTRS mechanism in sdk_event_handler.py already handles this IF the SDK emits streaming events — investigate whether the SDK can be configured to stream tool output, or whether we need to monitor child processes directly via psutil. Related: PokePoke-xe95e

title: Thread-unsafe shared collections in parallel worker pool — _futures dict, failed_claim_ids, current_active mutated across threads without synchronization
description:
## Summary

The parallel worker pool has **three shared mutable collections** accessed from both the main dispatch thread and ThreadPoolExecutor worker threads **without any synchronization primitive** (no threading.Lock, no RLock, no thread-safe container).

## Affected Files

- **src/pokepoke/agents/parallel_worker_pool.py** — \_futures: dict[Future, BeadsWorkItem]\ is exposed by reference via a property (line ~115) and mutated from dispatch (line ~177: \self._futures[fut] = item\) and collection (line ~70: \ utures.pop(fut)\) concurrently.
- **src/pokepoke/agents/parallel_support.py** — \ ailed_claim_ids: set[str]\ and \current_active: set[str]\ are passed by reference into \dispatch_items()\ and mutated from the main thread (lines ~231, ~244) while worker callbacks in \parallel_worker_pool.py\ (lines ~80-83) also add/discard from the same sets.

## Concrete Race Conditions

1. **Dict corruption**: Main thread calls \self._futures[fut] = item\ while \collect_done_futures()\ iterates and pops from the same dict → \RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration\
2. **Set lost updates**: Main thread adds item to \ ailed_claim_ids\ while worker thread discards same item → update silently lost, item incorrectly retried or skipped
3. **Stale snapshot**: \list(futures)\ snapshot races with concurrent \.pop()\ → KeyError or processing already-removed items

## Impact

- **Data corruption** in tracking structures under load (multiple parallel agents)
- **Duplicate work dispatch** (item dispatched twice if tracking set loses an update)
- **RuntimeError crashes** that terminate the parallel loop
- Most likely to manifest with pool_size >= 3 and fast-completing items

## Recommended Fix

Add a \	hreading.Lock\ to \ParallelWorkerPool\ and wrap all \_futures\ mutations. Pass the same lock to \dispatch_items()\ callers or use a thread-safe wrapper for \ ailed_claim_ids\ / \current_active\. Alternatively, route all mutations through the pool class methods that acquire the lock internally.

## Related

- PokePoke-wz1z2 covers config cache thread safety only — this is the parallel execution path, a different subsystem.

title: Orchestrator terminates when cleanup agent fails to resolve uncommitted changes
description: In run 20260219_160023_8eb732ff (icm_queue_c# repo), a maintenance agent (janitor or beta_tester) left uncommitted changes in the main repository. At 17:21:52 the orchestrator detected the dirty state and launched a cleanup agent. The cleanup agent ran for ~2 hours but failed at 19:22:00. The orchestrator then logged 'Cleanup agent failed to resolve uncommitted changes' and 'Main repo check failed', waited for 2 active workers to finish, and terminated the entire session. This is overly aggressive - a cleanup failure should not kill the whole orchestrator. The orchestrator should: (1) retry cleanup with a fresh agent, (2) stash or reset the uncommitted changes as a last resort, (3) continue processing work items even if the main repo has uncommitted changes (since workers use isolated worktrees). Impact: session ended prematurely after only 2/5 items completed, wasting ~2 hours of worker capacity.
close_reason: Fixed: Orchestrator now implements resilient cleanup recovery with 3 retries, stash fallback, and continue-on-failure since workers use isolated worktrees

title: Preflight repair git commit hangs indefinitely - pre-commit hooks block with 60s timeout
description: When launching the orchestrator (python -m pokepoke.orchestrator --autonomous --continuous --max-agents 2), preflight_repair.py attempts 'git commit -m chore: auto-commit for pre-flight health check' which triggers pre-commit hooks. The hooks take longer than the 60s subprocess timeout, causing TimeoutExpired. This retries twice and then crashes the orchestrator. Additionally, the pywebview WebView2 instance throws System.ObjectDisposedException ('Cannot access a disposed object') during shutdown, and fails to clean up its temp user data folder. Two issues: (1) preflight_repair.py L33 runs git commit with a 60s timeout but pre-commit hooks (tests, coverage, linting) can easily exceed that under load. Should either increase timeout, skip hooks for preflight auto-commits, or avoid committing during preflight entirely. (2) Desktop UI WebView2 disposal race: evaluate_js called after webview is already disposed, suggesting the UI thread and orchestrator thread shutdown ordering is wrong.

title: Make orchestration tests resilient to refactoring - reduce patch decorator coupling
description: Orchestration tests (test_orchestrator.py, test_workflow.py) use 16+ @patch decorators per test, each targeting exact internal module paths like @patch('pokepoke.workflow.run_gate_agent') and @patch('pokepoke.worktree_finalization.get_parent_id'). Fix: (1) Reduce patch count by injecting dependencies via function parameters or a context object instead of monkeypatching module-level imports. This ties into PokePoke-od1h (Protocol interfaces + DI). (2) Where patching is still needed, create shared mock factories (e.g. make_mock_workflow_deps()) that centralize the patch targets. (3) Test business logic decisions (retry count, item selection, state transitions) through the return values and state changes, not by asserting which internal functions were called. (4) Add a test helper that builds a minimal but real WorkItemResult/SessionStats so tests don't need to mock the entire object graph. title: Gate agent verdict lost on process force-kill due to output buffer race condition
description: Root cause: When the gate agent emits its JSON verdict and then the copilot CLI process idles with 158-byte heartbeat writes, the SDK watchdog eventually force-kills the process. There is a race condition in how the output buffer is captured at kill time: if the buffer is fully flushed, the gate JSON is found and parsed as SUCCESS; if in-flight or partially flushed, the result is classified as timeout/crash and the verdict is lost. This causes false FAILURE results on items where the gate actually approved the work. Evidence: PokePoke-575gv (SUCCESS) and PokePoke-30uwc (FAILURE) had identical behavior - gate emitted status:success JSON, process hung on heartbeats, force-killed. 575gv won the race, 30uwc lost it. Fix: In gate_agent_executor.py, parse the gate verdict JSON from the output buffer BEFORE checking result.success. If a valid status:success JSON block exists in output, return gate pass regardless of process exit status.
close_reason: Fixed: gate verdict is now parsed from output buffer before checking process exit status, preventing race condition on force-kill

title: Core orchestration modules have 0% test coverage despite being the critical execution path

1. Add integration-style tests that exercise real code paths with minimal mocking (mock only external I/O: subprocess, filesystem, beads CLI)

title: Git push in merge path missing TimeoutExpired handler and retry — causes unhandled crash and state corruption
description:
## Problem

`merge_worktree()` in `src/pokepoke/worktrees/worktrees.py` (lines 361-367) performs `git push` with a 120s timeout but:

1. **Missing `TimeoutExpired` handler (CRITICAL):** The except clause at line 364 only catches `CalledProcessError`. A push timeout raises `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` which propagates **unhandled** up the stack. The local merge is NOT rolled back because the rollback at line 366 is inside the `CalledProcessError` handler.

2. **No retry logic:** A single transient network failure permanently fails the merge. The retry infrastructure already exists for `git status` (`git_helpers.py:110-130` with exponential backoff) but is not used for push.

3. **Rollback can fail silently:** `_rollback_merge_commit()` (lines 293-300) catches its own errors and just logs them. If both push and rollback fail, the local repo has a merged commit that was never pushed and can't be reverted.

## Impact

**On push timeout (120s):**
- `TimeoutExpired` crashes through `perform_worktree_merge()` (unhandled)
- Local merge commit persists (not rolled back)
- Worktree cleanup status uncertain
- Remote doesn't have the commit
- **Result: Silent state corruption**

**On transient network error:**
- Rollback attempted but can fail
- Work item not marked done (good safeguard)
- But the local branch now has a committed merge that wasn't pushed
- No retry means transient failure is permanent

## Recommended Fix

1. Add `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` to the except clause at line 364
2. Add exponential backoff retry for `git push` (3 attempts, similar to `_run_git_status_with_retry`)
3. Consider extracting a `run_git_with_retry()` helper that works for any git command
4. If rollback fails after push failure, log CRITICAL and leave clear markers for manual intervention
5. Add test coverage for push timeout and network failure scenarios

## Files to modify
- `src/pokepoke/worktrees/worktrees.py` lines 361-367 — add TimeoutExpired handler + retry
- `src/pokepoke/git/git_helpers.py` — extract general retry helper
- `tests/worktrees/` — add push failure tests

title: Orchestrator stops launching agents after all 10 + janitor finish in continuous mode
description:
OBSERVED in run 20260223_103717_31235e8f (autonomous, continuous, max-agents=10):

TIMELINE:
- 10:37:17 - Orchestrator started, 10 parallel workers launched staggered (10:37-10:47)
- 10:48:28 - First worker completed. Tech debt agent starts.
- 10:49-10:51 - Workers 2-4 complete.
- 10:53:34 - Tech debt completed. Backlog cleanup tries to start but repo dirty (logProcessor.ts UU merge conflict + backfill_beads_item_stats.py untracked). Waits ~3min, times out, skipped.
- 10:56:35 - Code review also blocked by dirty repo (.pokepoke/config.yaml modified). Waits ~3min, times out, skipped.
- 10:59:42 - Auto-commit git add fails due to .git/index.lock (concurrent git process). Cleanup agent launched.
- 11:00-11:02 - Workers 5-6 complete.
- 11:06:05 - Cleanup agent resolves dirty state. Ready work fetched.
- 11:06:07 - Janitor Agent starts in maintenance slot.
- 11:06-11:27 - Workers 7-10 complete (some with 2 agent requests).
- 11:28:19 - Janitor Agent FAILED.
- 11:28:19 - Worktree cleanup tries to start but repo dirty (8 files, UU StatsPage.tsx merge conflict). Waits ~3min, times out, skipped.
- 11:31:21 - Worktree cleanup skipped. Session counter logs 3 then 4 (not 10).
- 11:31:21 - Janitor maintenance tries again but repo still dirty (8 files).
- LOG ENDS AT LINE 465 mid-janitor-dirty-wait. No shutdown message, no continuous loop restart.

ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS:
1. After all 10 workers + maintenance finished, orchestrator should loop back to fetch ready work and launch a new batch. Instead the log just stops - no continuous loop iteration occurred.
2. Persistently dirty repo (UU merge conflicts from concurrent worker merges) blocked ALL maintenance agents (backlog_cleanup, code_review, worktree_cleanup, janitor) - each waited ~3min then skipped.
3. .git/index.lock contention happened during the run from concurrent git operations.
4. Orchestrator process exited with code 1 - likely crashed or exited after maintenance phase without triggering continuous loop.
5. No graceful shutdown log entry - consistent with an unhandled exit path.

CONTRIBUTING FACTORS:
- Merge conflicts (UU status files) left by workers are never cleaned up, permanently blocking maintenance
- The janitor agent itself failed, which may have been the trigger for orchestrator to exit instead of loop
- Session counter shows wrong count (3, 4 instead of 10) suggesting possible state tracking bug

title: Code Review: process_work_item cleanup crashes before metrics import
description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. Trigger any exception in process_work_item before the inline import executes (e.g., make get_config() or select_model_for_item() raise).
2. The function exits through the finally block, which unconditionally calls set_current_work_item_id(None).
3. Because the import never ran, the name is undefined and Python raises UnboundLocalError instead of the original failure, so cleanup/unassign never runs.

Impact:
- The real root cause is masked by UnboundLocalError, so operators cannot see why startup failed.
- The finally block aborts before cleanup_worktree/unassign logic executes, leaving worktrees dirty and beads items stuck as assigned.
- Any early failure in workflow.process_work_item now wedges the system.

Code reference:
- src/pokepoke/workflow.py lines 52-75 import set_current_work_item_id inside the try block, but lines 272-279 in the finally block always call it.

Suggested fix:
- Import set_current_work_item_id at module scope (or before the try) so the name is always bound, or guard the cleanup call.

title: Decomposition agent timeout of 120s is too short
description: The decomposition agent (_DECOMPOSITION_TIMEOUT) is set to 120 seconds. This agent needs to: (1) read the work item and failure history, (2) explore the codebase to understand the scope of the item, (3) analyze why previous attempts failed, (4) determine a logical split into independently completable subtasks with correct scoping. The decomposition agent should have a timeout more aligned with the work agent timeout, or at minimum 5-10 minutes. A bad decomposition (from being rushed by timeout) is worse than no decomposition — it creates subtasks that are either still too large, overlap in scope, or miss dependencies. Increase _DECOMPOSITION_TIMEOUT and make it configurable via pokepoke.config.json.

title: Model stats file corruption under multi-process concurrent writes
description: model_stats_store.py record_completion() uses a threading.Lock (_lock) to serialize read-modify-write of the JSON stats file (lines 137-141). This protects against concurrent threads within a single process, but in multi-agent mode with --max-agents > 1, multiple worker PROCESSES can race on the same file. Two processes can both read, modify, and write the stats file, causing the second write to overwrite the first's changes (lost update). The atomic os.replace() on line 129 prevents corruption but not lost records. Fix: use the existing filelock-based coordination system (coordination.py acquire_lock) to serialize cross-process access, or switch to an append-only JSONL format that avoids read-modify-write entirely.
