title: Orchestrator must serialize non-parallel items and drain fleet for maintenance agents
description:
Two scheduling improvements needed:

1. NON-PARALLEL ITEMS: When a work item cannot run in parallel (e.g. items touching shared code areas), the orchestrator must wait until no other agents are in_progress before scheduling that item. Currently it spawns agents without checking for parallelism conflicts.

title: Worktree finally-block cleanup ignores finalized_successfully — risks force-deleting unmerged branches
description:
## Problem

In `workflow.py` lines 342-348, the `finally` block unconditionally calls `cleanup_worktree(item.id, force=True)` regardless of whether `finalized_successfully` is True:

```python
finally:
    try:
        if worktree_path is not None:
            cleanup_worktree(item.id, force=True)
```

The `finalized_successfully` flag IS checked on line 350 for unassignment, but the cleanup call above runs unconditionally with `force=True`.

## Impact

- After successful finalization (which already merges and cleans up), this redundantly calls cleanup. Currently benign because cleanup handles already-removed worktrees.
- If an exception occurs DURING the merge phase (between checkout and merge completion), `force=True` causes `git branch -D` (force delete), permanently losing committed but unmerged work.
- In parallel mode, this is more likely due to timing issues and resource contention.

## Fix

Guard cleanup with the existing flag:

```python
if worktree_path is not None and not finalized_successfully:
    cleanup_worktree(item.id, force=True)
```

## Files
- `src/pokepoke/workflow.py` lines 342-348
close_reason: Closed

title: Gate agent approves but workflow marks as rejected - JSON verdict parsing fails
description:
In run 20260223_161755_8b609828, PokePoke-sqyp gate agent output NEW_WORK_VERIFIED with 'All verification steps passed' but the workflow treated it as rejected with 'Gate Agent did not explicitly approve the fix. Check logs.' This caused an unnecessary retry (v2).

Root cause: run_gate_agent() in agent_runner.py L89-121 failed to parse the gate agent JSON verdict. The regex r'`json\s*(\{.*?\})\s*`' uses a non-greedy single-line match that likely fails on multiline JSON objects. The text fallback only checks for 'VERIFICATION SUCCESSFUL' literal text and does NOT check for 'NEW_WORK_VERIFIED' or other valid approval reasons. So when the JSON regex misses the verdict, the function falls through to line 121 returning False with 'Gate Agent did not explicitly approve the fix.'

Additionally, there was a concurrent 'Error checking git status' from cleanup_agents.py:35 where verify_main_repo_clean() threw RuntimeError during the cleanup loop (likely git status --porcelain failed due to concurrent git operations across parallel worktrees).

Fix candidates:
1. Use re.DOTALL flag in the JSON regex so it matches multiline JSON blocks
2. Add 'NEW_WORK_VERIFIED' and other gate verdict status strings to the text fallback check
3. Consider parsing the structured verdict from log lines (already implemented in frontend parseGateVerdict)
4. Investigate why git status --porcelain failed in worktree context (possible concurrent git contention)

title: Make gate rejections panel collapsible on stats page
All 9 retry/backoff sites lack jitter — synchronized retry storms under parallel operation
description: RetryConfig in types.py:77-83 declares 'jitter: bool = True' but this field is NEVER consumed by any retry implementation. All 9 retry locations use bare exponential backoff without jitter: (1) git_helpers.py:126 _run_git_status_with_retry, (2) cli_retry.py:100 _run_bd_with_retry, (3) beads_recovery.py:103, (4-5) sync_strategy.py:151,225, (6) worktree_cleanup.py:191, (7) file_utils.py:17, (8) manifest_utils.py:89, (9) preflight_repair.py:226. Under parallel operation with N agents, when a transient error occurs (index.lock contention, bd daemon timeout, file lock), ALL agents compute identical backoff delays and wake simultaneously, re-contending the same resource. This is the classic thundering herd anti-pattern. With 10 parallel agents hitting index.lock, they all sleep 0.5s, wake together, all retry, all fail, all sleep 1s, wake together again. FIX: Create a shared retry helper that consumes RetryConfig and applies jitter (e.g. delay * random.uniform(0.5, 1.5)). Replace all 9 bare time.sleep(delay) patterns with this helper. The RetryConfig.jitter flag already exists — just wire it up.

title: shutdown.py request_shutdown blocks signal handler for up to 180s
description: request_shutdown() in shutdown.py calls merge_queue.shutdown(timeout=180.0) synchronously inside the signal handler. This blocks the signal handler thread for up to 180 seconds waiting for the merge queue to drain, making the process appear unresponsive to the user during shutdown. Consider making shutdown non-blocking (e.g. set a flag and let main loop drain) or reducing the timeout significantly.

title: Implement Spec Registry pattern for agent codebase knowledge (inspired by CPCS.CollectorDownTesting)
description: Instead of a static project index file that gets stale, implement a Spec Registry pattern (as used by the CPCS.CollectorDownTesting team in msazure/One). KEY CONCEPT: Specs are curated markdown files in docs/specs/ that map business outcomes and requirements to collaborating code components. They capture WHERE to find code and WHY it exists, not WHAT it does. An INDEX.yaml catalog provides fast discovery. Agents consult the index BEFORE exploring code, dramatically reducing exploration tokens. CRITICAL DIFFERENCES from a static project index: (1) Specs are maintained by agents as a side-effect of normal work — when an agent learns something non-trivial about component interactions, it writes/updates a spec automatically; (2) Specs have confidence levels (high/medium/low) and staleness tracking (90-day expiry); (3) Discovery is index-based, not full-scan — agents read INDEX.yaml, match against task description, open only top 1-3 matches; (4) Writes are triggered only for non-trivial interactions (not bug fixes or minor refactors); (5) No-op guard prevents unnecessary rewrites. IMPLEMENTATION: (1) Create docs/specs/ directory with INDEX.yaml; (2) Add spec-registry.instructions.md with applyTo src/** for Copilot CLI agents; (3) Seed initial specs from existing codebase knowledge (orchestrator, beads integration, worktree management, validation engine, etc.); (4) Add agent-spawn-optimization instructions that require parent agents to pre-gather context before spawning sub-agents. REFERENCE: See C:\Users\ameliapayne\CPCS.CollectorDownTesting\.github\instructions\spec-registry.instructions.md for the full pattern.

title: Worktree resource leak on unhandled exceptions in workflow.py
description:
In workflow.py process_work_item(), the finally block (line 256-258) only calls unregister_agent() but does NOT clean up the worktree. If any unhandled exception occurs between worktree creation (line 91, via _setup_worktree) and the explicit cleanup calls in the success/failure branches (lines 196/238), the worktree persists indefinitely on disk.

This is a resource leak that compounds over time: each orphaned worktree consumes disk space and leaves stale git branch metadata. In autonomous continuous mode, this can exhaust disk space.

Fix: Add worktree cleanup to the finally block:

finally:
    try:
        if worktree_path is not None:
            cleanup_worktree(item.id, force=True)
    except Exception:
        pass  # Best-effort cleanup
    unregister_agent()

Key file: src/pokepoke/workflow.py, lines 256-258
Severity: Critical - cumulative resource leak in autonomous operation

title: Signal handler calls async-unsafe code in request_shutdown - deadlock risk
description:
The signal handler _signal_handler() in signal_handlers.py calls request_shutdown() from shutdown.py. This function performs multiple async-signal-unsafe operations that can cause permanent deadlock:

1. NON-REENTRANT LOCK (DEADLOCK): request_shutdown() acquires _agent_count_lock (threading.Lock, line 85). In single-agent mode, the main thread calls register_agent()/unregister_agent()/get_active_agent_count() which also acquire this lock. If SIGINT/SIGTERM fires while the main thread holds _agent_count_lock, the signal handler tries to re-acquire it causing permanent deadlock (threading.Lock is not reentrant).

Reproduction: Main thread enters get_active_agent_count() -> acquires _agent_count_lock -> SIGINT fires -> signal handler calls request_shutdown() -> tries with _agent_count_lock -> DEADLOCK.

2. DYNAMIC MODULE IMPORT: 'from pokepoke.merge_queue import get_merge_queue' inside signal handler path. If signal fires during any import operation, Python import machinery can deadlock.

3. THREAD CREATION: threading.Thread().start() starts watchdog thread from signal context.

4. COMPLEX METHOD CALLS: _executor.shutdown() and merge_queue.signal_stop() acquire their own internal locks.

Files: src/pokepoke/signal_handlers.py (lines 93-95), src/pokepoke/shutdown.py (line 85)

Fix options (in order of preference):
- Best: signal handler only sets _shutdown_event and returns. Move ALL complex shutdown logic (merge queue, watchdog, executor, lock reads) to the main loop shutdown path.
- Better: make request_shutdown() signal-safe by reading _active_agent_count without a lock and moving imports to module level.
- Minimum: replace _agent_count_lock = threading.Lock() with threading.RLock() to fix the lock deadlock specifically.

title: Parallel agent worktree creation lacks coordination - race condition causes mass failures
description:
## Problem

During parallel agent execution, worktree creation is not properly coordinated. When multiple agents (up to 10) launch simultaneously and attempt to create their worktrees, 9 out of 10 fail with unspecified errors.

## Impact

- Critical failure rate (90% failure) in parallel mode
- All agents except the first one fail to even start processing work items
- No agent requests are made because agents fail during initialization
- Run: C:\Users\ameliapayne\icm_queue_c#\.pokepoke\logs\20260224_150927_b72ade52
  - Workers 2-10 all failed to create worktrees
  - Only worker-1 successfully created its worktree

## Root Cause

Worktree creation likely has a race condition preventing coordination between concurrent agent processes. The worktree setup code may not be using proper locking or atomic operations when creating multiple worktrees simultaneously.

## Suggested Fix

- Add file-based locking mechanism for worktree creation sequence
- Implement atomic worktree creation with proper synchronization
- Ensure worktree creation serializes operations to .git/worktrees directory
- Add logging to trace actual worktree creation failures
close_reason: Closed

Details: open_project(path) currently os.chdir()'s to the provided path (desktop_api_ext.py:315) and uses that same path to check for .pokepoke (line 312). If the user picks a subdirectory inside a git repo, this will incorrectly report needs_init=True and may load config from the repo root while leaving cwd at the subdir; the requirement explicitly calls for updating cwd/repo root, which implies resolving the git top-level (e.g., git rev-parse --show-toplevel) and switching to that. Also, there is no explicit beads availability/initialization/reinit step (e.g., running/validating bd info or providing a needs_beads_init signal) despite the requirement to reinitialize beads connection; changing cwd alone doesn’t guarantee beads is initialized for the selected repo. Finally, open_project resets some DesktopAPI fields but does not clear the AgentRegistry or reset the global stop-after-current flag, so prior session UI/state can bleed into the new project.

title: Rewrite copilot_sdk fallback retry - shared mutable state across module boundaries is fragile
description: copilot_sdk.py send_with_retry() uses nonlocal to mutate 7+ outer variables, while sdk_event_handler.py signals fallback via dictionary mutation (stats['tried_fallback']). The control flow crosses module boundaries via shared mutable dict. There is a race condition between done.set() in the error handler and the retry check in send_with_retry(). The fallback retry may never actually trigger, or may trigger unpredictably depending on event ordering. Fix: Replace shared-mutable-state approach with an explicit retry loop that catches a typed RateLimitError exception, rather than using dictionary mutation across module boundaries.

title: Code Review: stress tests don't verify thread joins
description: tests/agents/test_parallel_stress.py lines 200-224 and 590-612 call Thread.join(timeout=5) but never check whether the thread actually finished. If a writer/reader thread blocks, join returns after the timeout and the test still passes while the hung thread keeps running. That masks deadlocks and can leak live threads into later tests. After each join(timeout) call, check thread.is_alive() (or the boolean return) and fail the test when a thread misses the deadline. This ensures the stress tests actually detect liveness regressions.

title: Agent infinite-loops on hung powershell commands instead of killing and retrying
description: When a command run via the agent's powershell tool hangs (e.g. pytest without --timeout), the agent enters an infinite read_powershell loop, calling it repeatedly with increasing delays (60s, 120s, 300s) but never kills the process or tries a different approach. In PokePoke-4yaq, the agent wasted ~25 minutes calling read_powershell 9 times on a hung pytest before the session timed out with FAILURE. The agent needs: (1) A max_retries or cumulative_timeout policy for read_powershell - after N retries or M total seconds, automatically stop_powershell and report a timeout error. (2) The corrective feedback loop should kick in, telling the agent the command timed out and suggesting it retry with a timeout flag or run targeted tests. (3) Consider adding a configurable command_timeout to the orchestrator config that auto-kills any command exceeding it.

title: Use a dedicated merge worktree instead of the main repo for merges
description: Currently all merges happen in the main repo working tree because git merge requires the target branch checked out, and master is checked out in the main repo. This couples PokePoke's merge operations to the user's working directory, causing: (1) steps 2/3b must clean up the main repo before merging, (2) the user can't work in the main repo while a merge is in progress, (3) any dirty state in the main repo blocks merges, (4) the cleanup agent operates on the main repo which is risky. Proposed: create a dedicated merge worktree (e.g. worktrees/.merge-target) that permanently has master checked out. The main repo sits on a detached HEAD or a dummy branch. All merges (checkout, merge --no-ff, validate) happen in the merge worktree instead. Benefits: (a) main repo working tree is never touched by PokePoke merges, (b) no need for main repo dirty checks or cleanup agents before merge, (c) user can freely work in main repo during autonomous operation, (d) merge worktree is always clean by construction since only PokePoke writes to it, (e) still needs the merge lock (concurrent merges in the merge worktree would still conflict). The merge worktree would be created once during init/startup and reused across all merges.
close_reason: Completed by PokePoke orchestrator (agent did not close)

title: Code Review: merge conflict cleanup fallback waits on its own lock
description: In src/pokepoke/cleanup_agents.py (around lines 340-350) invoke_merge_conflict_cleanup_agent() falls back to invoke_cleanup_agent() when merge-conflict prompt loading fails. The fallback call ignores the incoming wait_for_merge flag and always uses the default wait_for_merge=True. When perform_worktree_merge() calls invoke_merge_conflict_cleanup_agent(..., wait_for_merge=False) it already holds merge_lock; if the prompt is missing/corrupt the fallback now calls _wait_for_merge_completion() while the same thread still owns the lock. That busy-waits for the full 10 minute timeout before proceeding, effectively freezing merges and spamming

title: Implement WorkItemSession.__exit__ success path and _verify_post_release_state
description:
Implement the success exit path in WorkItemSession (exc_type is None) and the post-release verification.

Success path steps:
1. write_journal(MERGING)
2. acquire merge_lock()
3. verify_worktree_clean() — raise SessionError if dirty state detected
4. merge_worktree_into_main() — raise SessionError on conflict/fail
5. write_journal(CLEANING)
6. remove_worktree(force=True) — log ERROR if fails; continue
7. delete_branch() — log ERROR if fails; continue
8. close_beads_item() — log ERROR if fails; continue
9. _verify_post_release_state()
10. write_journal(CLOSED) then delete_journal()

_verify_post_release_state() checks all four invariants:
- worktree directory does not exist on disk
- branch is absent from git branch --list
- .git/MERGE_HEAD does not exist (repo not mid-merge)
- beads item status == 'closed'
Any failure: log ERROR, leave journal in CLEANING phase for reconciler.

All failures in __exit__ logged at ERROR (not debug/warning). None swallowed silently.

title: get_issue_dependencies() missing error handling crashes orchestrator on malformed beads output
description:
Problem:
`_parse_beads_json()` (beads_query.py:92) can raise `json.JSONDecodeError`, and `get_issue_dependencies()` (beads_query.py:161) calls it without any try/except. Additionally, line 165 accesses `issues_data[0]` without checking if the result is a non-empty list, risking `IndexError` or `TypeError`.

Blast radius:
- `has_unmet_blocking_dependencies()` (beads_query.py:198) calls `get_issue_dependencies()` without error handling
- `work_item_selection.py:56` calls `has_unmet_blocking_dependencies()` in a loop over ALL ready items
- `beads_hierarchy.py` calls `get_issue_dependencies()` at 4 call sites (lines 38, 54, 309, 331), only one of which (line 331) wraps in try/except
- One malformed beads item during work item selection propagates an unhandled exception through the entire call chain, terminating the orchestrator session (caught at orchestrator.py:373 `except Exception`, which prints error and returns exit code 1)

In continuous autonomous mode, this means one bad item kills the entire session.

The correct pattern already exists in this codebase at `get_ready_work_items()` (beads_query.py:133-141):
`python
try:
    items_data = _parse_beads_json(result.stdout)
    ...
except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError) as e:
    logger.warning(...)
    return []

Fix: Wrap the `_parse_beads_json()` call and `issues_data[0]` access in `get_issue_dependencies()` in try/except, returning None on failure. Also wrap the unprotected calls in `beads_hierarchy.py` (lines 38, 54, 309) or make `get_issue_dependencies()` itself safe. Estimated effort: ~30 minutes.

title: signal_handlers.py: _signal_handler calls sys.exit() without request_shutdown(), bypassing graceful shutdown
description:
## Problem

In signal_handlers.py line 94, _signal_handler() calls sys.exit(exit_code) directly without first calling request_shutdown() from shutdown.py. This completely bypasses the graceful shutdown coordination system.

### What request_shutdown() does that is skipped:
1. Sets the global _shutdown_event (line 63) — agents check this to stop work
2. Calls _executor.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True) (line 67) — stops ThreadPoolExecutor
3. Calls merge_queue.shutdown(30.0) (line 77) — drains pending merges
4. Starts a watchdog thread with scaled timeout (line 92) — ensures eventual hard exit

### What sys.exit() does instead:
- Raises SystemExit in the main thread only
- Daemon threads (merge queue worker, agent threads) are killed immediately
- No opportunity to drain the merge queue or finish in-progress merges

### Impact in parallel agent mode:
- If SIGINT/SIGTERM arrives during a merge operation, the merge queue daemon thread is killed mid-operation
- This can leave the repository in a partially-merged state (dirty working tree, uncommitted changes on target branch)
- Orphaned worktrees may not be tracked in the cleanup manifest
- Active agent subprocesses (copilot CLI) may become zombies since they aren't signaled

### Recommended Fix:
In _signal_handler(), call request_shutdown() before sys.exit():
```
def _signal_handler(signum, frame):
    # ... logging ...
    from pokepoke.shutdown import request_shutdown
    request_shutdown()
    sys.exit(128 + signum)
```

This ensures the merge queue is drained and agents are signaled before the process exits. The watchdog in request_shutdown() provides a hard-exit fallback if graceful shutdown stalls.
close_reason: Closed

title: ExplicitSync.sync() return value masks git publish failures from callers
description:
## Problem

In \src/pokepoke/beads/sync_strategy.py\, \ExplicitSync.sync()\ returns the \ r sync\ CompletedProcess result (returncode 0 on success) even when the subsequent \_git_publish_sync()\ fails. The git add/commit/push failure is logged as a warning (line 262) but never reflected in the return value.

This means \ssign_and_sync_item()\ in \ eads_management.py\ (line 180) sees \sync_result.returncode == 0\ and prints the misleading success message:
\\\
Synced assignment - other agents will see {item_id} is claimed
\\\
...when in fact the assignment was NOT published and remote agents CANNOT see the claim. The warning path at lines 183-184 (designed for exactly this scenario) is never triggered for the br backend.

## Impact

- **Duplicate work item assignment** in multi-machine deployments using \ r\ backend
- **Wasted compute** when two agents work the same item
- **Merge conflicts** when both agents try to merge their results
- **Misleading operational logs** — operators see success when sync actually failed

## Root Cause

\ExplicitSync.sync()\ at line 200-207 returns \esult\ (the \ r sync\ CompletedProcess) after calling \self._git_publish_sync()\, regardless of whether git publish succeeded. The \_git_publish_sync()\ method (line 228-262) catches all errors and only logs a warning.

## Suggested Fix

Option A (minimal): Have \_git_publish_sync()\ return a bool indicating success, and set a non-zero returncode on the CompletedProcess if publish failed:
\\\python
if not self._git_publish_sync():
    result = subprocess.CompletedProcess(result.args, 1, result.stdout, 'git publish failed')
\\\

Option B (better): Return a richer result type (e.g. \SyncResult\ dataclass) with separate \sync_ok\ and \publish_ok\ fields so callers can handle each failure mode appropriately.

## Files

- \src/pokepoke/beads/sync_strategy.py\ lines 200-262
- \src/pokepoke/beads/beads_management.py\ lines 175-185
- \	ests/beads/test_sync_strategy.py\ lines 296-316 (tests verify no crash but don't assert return value accuracy)

title: Remove process-global agent identity fallback from parallel execution paths
description:
Problem: agent identity resolution still falls back to process-global state via os.environ['AGENT_NAME'], even though the repo introduced thread-local agent context for parallel agents. This keeps hidden coupling between threads and sequential code paths and makes behavior dependent on ambient process state.

Evidence:
- src/pokepoke/agents/agent_context.py resolves agent name from thread-local first, then os.environ['AGENT_NAME']
- src/pokepoke/orchestration/orchestrator.py sets os.environ['AGENT_NAME'] at startup
- src/pokepoke/agents/parallel.py and related code call set_agent_name() for workers, but many downstream call sites still use get_agent_name() with implicit fallback

Impact:
- Hidden reliance on ambient environment makes concurrent behavior harder to reason about
- AI-authored refactors can accidentally preserve or reintroduce cross-thread identity leaks
- Tests may pass because of process-global fallback rather than because identity is being propagated correctly

Requested outcome:
1. Define a single explicit agent identity propagation model
2. Remove or minimize reliance on os.environ['AGENT_NAME'] for runtime behavior, especially in parallel flows
3. Make worker identity an explicit parameter or context object at critical boundaries
4. Add tests proving parallel workers cannot observe the wrong agent identity through fallback state

Acceptance criteria:
- Parallel execution does not depend on process-global AGENT_NAME for correctness
- Agent identity at critical boundaries is explicit and testable
- Remaining fallback behavior, if any, is tightly scoped and documented
- Tests cover both sequential and parallel identity propagation without ambient-state leakage

title: Silent manifest save failure in worktree_cleanup.py loses orphaned worktree tracking
description:
In worktree_cleanup.py save_worktree_manifest() (lines 81-89), OSError exceptions are silently swallowed with pass. When add_uncleaned_worktree() calls save_worktree_manifest() and the save fails, the worktree entry is lost from the tracking manifest permanently. The orphaned worktree remains on disk but has no tracking record, so automatic cleanup will never find it.

Current code (lines 88-89):
  except OSError:
      pass  # Silently fail to avoid disrupting main operations

Impact: In long-running autonomous sessions, disk space slowly leaks as orphaned worktrees accumulate without tracking. The manifest is the ONLY mechanism for discovering worktrees that need cleanup after failed operations. Silent failure here means those worktrees are invisible to the cleanup system.

Fix: Log the failure so operators can diagnose the issue, and consider a retry or fallback path:
  except OSError as e:
      logger.warning('Failed to save worktree manifest: %s', e)
      # Worktree at %s may become orphaned

title: Rebase abort failures silently swallowed in merge queue - no logging or state verification
description:
In merge_queue.py `_rebase_worktree()` (lines 261-272, 276-288), when `git rebase --abort` fails after a failed rebase, the exception is caught with a bare `pass` - no logging, no error recording, no state verification.

Code at lines 271-272 and 286-287:
`python
except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
    pass  # SILENT - no logging
``n
After this silent failure, `_rebase_worktree` returns False. Then `_process_request` (line 170-173) logs a warning and proceeds to call `merge_worktree_to_dev()` on a worktree that may be in a broken mid-rebase state.

While the downstream `is_worktree_clean()` check in `merge_worktree()` would catch a dirty worktree, the complete lack of logging means:
1. Engineers debugging merge failures have no evidence that rebase aborts are failing
2. Recurring rebase abort failures (e.g., from git lock contention) go undetected
3. No metrics or alerts can be built on this failure mode

**Fix:**
1. Log a warning when rebase abort fails (the exception details are critical for debugging)
2. Verify worktree state after abort failure before returning
3. Consider returning a richer result indicating abort-failure vs clean-failure

title: Model selection ignores registry - always uses default/fallback when candidate_models is empty

The _filter_available_models() function only FILTERS an existing candidate list against the registry - it never POPULATES the list from registry data. This means the entire model sync/discovery pipeline (which correctly discovers 17+ available models) has zero effect on actual model selection. The fix: when candidate_models is empty and weighted selection is active, use get_available_model_names() from the registry as the candidate pool instead of just default+fallback.

comments.text:
## Problem

Overall test coverage is 24%. The following **core orchestration modules** have literally **0% test coverage**:

| Module | Statements | Coverage | Risk |
|--------|-----------|----------|------|
| orchestrator.py | 279 | 0% | Entry point, session lifecycle |
| parallel.py | 242 | 0% | Concurrent agent dispatch, ThreadPoolExecutor |

| merge_queue.py | 174 | 0% | Serialized merge coordination |
| worktree_merge_handler.py | 99 | 0% | Merge retry logic |
| work_item_selection.py | 104 | 0% | Item prioritization/selection |

These modules handle the most complex and error-prone parts of the system: concurrent dispatch, worktree lifecycle, and merge serialization. The pre-commit hook only enforces 80% coverage on **modified** files, so these modules can accumulate regressions indefinitely without detection.

## Impact

- Any regression in the parallel loop or merge queue goes undetected until production failure
- Refactoring these modules is extremely risky without test coverage
- The 80% pre-commit gate creates a false sense of safety since it doesn't apply to unmodified files

## Recommendation

Priority order for adding tests:
1. **workflow.py** - The core work processing pipeline; most business logic lives here
2. **parallel.py** - Concurrent dispatch logic; thread safety bugs are the hardest to debug
3. **merge_queue.py** - Serialized merge coordination; data integrity depends on this
4. **orchestrator.py** - Entry point; can start with integration-style tests

Focus on testing:
- Happy path through process_work_item (workflow.py)
- Concurrent agent slot management (parallel.py)
- Merge queue ordering and shutdown drain (merge_queue.py)
- Error recovery paths (worktree failures, claim conflicts)

title: Release merge lock during conflict resolution agent, re-acquire for retry
description: After git merge --abort (step 11i) the main repo is clean and identical to pre-lock state. The conflict cleanup agent (step 11k) only modifies the isolated worktree branch. title: Silent merge rollback failure leaves repo with unpushed merge commit
description:
In worktrees.py, _rollback_merge_commit() (lines 293-311) returns a bool indicating success/failure, but ALL THREE callers (lines 363, 367, 385) ignore the return value and return (False, []) regardless. If git reset --hard HEAD~1 fails (disk full, permissions, git corruption), the merged commit remains in the local repo unpushed, and no caller is informed.

Impact: Repository corruption. A failed rollback after post-merge validation failure or push failure leaves a dangling local merge commit. The next merge from another worker may encounter stale branch state, and no automated recovery kicks in because the caller received the same (False, []) as a successful rollback.

Scenario: (1) execute_merge_sequence succeeds locally, (2) validate_post_merge fails, (3) _rollback_merge_commit fails (returns False), (4) caller ignores False and returns (False, []) to orchestrator, (5) repo now has unpushed merge commit with no tracking or recovery.

Existing test test_push_failure_reset_failure_does_not_raise (line 1886) confirms the function does not raise on double failure but does NOT verify that corruption state is propagated. The function's own tests (lines 2078-2098) verify it returns True/False correctly, but no test covers the caller's handling of False.

Fix: All three call sites must check the return value. On False, either (a) set a repo-corrupted flag that triggers manual intervention or preflight repair on next run, or (b) call preflight_repair.attempt_repo_recovery() immediately. The (False, []) return should be augmented to a 3-tuple (False, [], rollback_failed=True) or use a dataclass result.

Location: src/pokepoke/worktrees/worktrees.py lines 360-368 (post-merge validation), lines 379-386 (push failure)

title: Code Review: Model sync ignores disable flag
description:
## Problem
The orchestrator now calls sync_copilot_models(force=True) at startup (see src/pokepoke/orchestration/orchestrator.py lines 188-192). Passing  orce=True bypasses _should_skip_sync, which is the only place that honors model_sync.enabled. As a result, even when the config sets model_sync.enabled: false, the sync still runs and executes all the side effects added in sync_copilot_models (beads create/update/close, config pruning, bd sync). Prior to this change the sync respected the flag and skipped entirely.

## Impact
* Operators who disable model sync (e.g., missing Copilot CLI, offline environments, custom model lists) now have that setting ignored.
* The forced run can mutate .pokepoke/config.yaml via prune_unavailable_from_config and close beads issues even though the feature is disabled, leading to data loss.
* Runs happen every startup because the orchestrator always forces them, defeating the point of the interval knob.

## Suggested Fix
Ensure model_sync.enabled is honored even when forcing a run. Either keep the enabled check outside the force shortcut, or only skip the interval check when forcing. At minimum, the orchestrator should check the config before invoking the sync.
close_reason: Fixed: Model sync now respects enabled flag even when force=True is passed. The enabled check was moved to the start of sync_copilot_models() before the force logic, ensuring operators can disable model sync and have that setting honored. Added comprehensive tests to verify the fix works correctly in both forced and normal modes.

title: Parallel workers sharing same beads item collide on UI agent_id, showing wrong failed status
description:
When the orchestrator assigns multiple parallel workers to the same beads work item (e.g. a re-attempt while an earlier worker is still running), both workers share agent_id = item.id in the UI panel.

Observed in run 20260219_125559_5d130fb2:
- worker-4 started item beads_ui-e2md at ~12:56:43 (thread-pool queued), actually began executing at 13:09:37
- worker-5 was submitted for the same item at 13:09:37 while worker-4 was in-flight
- worker-5 failed immediately at 13:10:58 with 0 agent requests
- Because both use push_agent_status(agent_id=item.id), worker-5's 'failed' push overwrote worker-4's slot in the UI
- The UI showed the item as FAILED while worker-4 was still actively writing files until 13:22:30

Root cause: In parallel.py line 49, agent_id = item.id. Two threads working on the same item have identical agent_ids, so the later failure clobbers the first worker's live status.

Fix: Use a unique agent_id that incorporates the worker name (e.g. worker_agent_name or hash of item.id + worker counter) so each parallel slot has its own UI row.

title: Worktree creation errors visible in UI but not written to file logs
description: Problem: In run 20260224_171341, 11 items failed with 0 agent requests. The user saw worktree creation errors in the desktop UI but these errors were absent from orchestrator.log and item log files. Root cause: _setup_worktree() in workflow.py (L358) catches worktree creation exceptions and calls print() which is intercepted by desktop_ui.py _print_redirect into an in-memory buffer (polled by the frontend), but never writes to RunLogger or ItemLogger. The caller at L114-120 then calls _log_failure() which only writes a generic Status: FAILURE with no context about what failed. Logging architecture gap: print() goes to in-memory UI buffer (never persisted to disk); logger.error() (stdlib) goes to stderr/console (not connected to RunLogger); only RunLogger.log_orchestrator() and ItemLogger.log_error() write to .pokepoke/logs/. Fix: (1) Pass run_logger and item_logger to _setup_worktree() in workflow.py. (2) On worktree creation failure, call both run_logger.log_orchestrator(error, level=ERROR) and item_logger.log_error(error). (3) Include the full exception traceback, not just the message. (4) Audit other print()-based error paths in workflow.py and parallel.py for the same gap. Files: src/pokepoke/workflow.py (L114-120, L358), src/pokepoke/worktrees.py, src/pokepoke/desktop_ui.py (L80).

title: has_uncommitted_changes() returns False on git failure, risking data loss during merge
description:
In git_operations.py line 41-51, has_uncommitted_changes() catches CalledProcessError and TimeoutExpired and returns False - falsely reporting the repo is clean. This function is called before merge operations to verify repo state.

**The bug:** If git is temporarily unavailable, slow, or the repo is in a bad state, the function reports 'no uncommitted changes' when it actually couldn't check. Downstream merge logic proceeds as if the repo is clean, potentially overwriting uncommitted work.

**Fix:** Either raise the exception to let callers handle it, or return a tri-state (True/False/Unknown):

\\\python
def has_uncommitted_changes(cwd: Optional[str] = None) -> bool:
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ['git', 'status', '--porcelain'],
            capture_output=True, text=True, encoding='utf-8',
            errors='replace', check=True, timeout=10, cwd=cwd
        )
        return bool(result.stdout.strip())
    except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as e:
        # Safer: assume dirty if we can't verify
        logger.warning('Could not check uncommitted changes: %s', e)
        return True  # Assume dirty to prevent data loss
\\\

**Impact:** Data loss during autonomous merge operations when git is temporarily unavailable.

title: Thread-unsafe os.environ mutation in copilot_sdk.py causes encoding corruption
description: copilot_sdk.py modifies os.environ['PYTHONIOENCODING'] globally (lines 64-65, 420-423) without any synchronization. With parallel agents (max_parallel_agents > 1), multiple threads call invoke_copilot_sdk concurrently. Thread A sets PYTHONIOENCODING='utf-8:replace', Thread B restores the original value, Thread A's copilot process inherits the wrong encoding. This causes UnicodeDecodeError crashes or garbled output in concurrent agent runs. Related to PokePoke-furd (per-agent env isolation) but this is a specific data-corruption bug that needs immediate attention. Fix: Use subprocess env parameter to pass PYTHONIOENCODING only to the child process instead of modifying the global os.environ. Example: env = {**os.environ, 'PYTHONIOENCODING': 'utf-8:replace'} passed via client options.

title: Data persistence stores (stats, model history) have 0% coverage risking silent data corruption
description:
Three data persistence modules have 0% test coverage:
- beads_item_stats_store.py (100 stmts) - stores per-item statistics
- model_stats_store.py (125 stmts) - stores model performance data  
- beads_item_stats_backfill.py (85 stmts) - backfills historical stats

These modules write persistent state to disk. Bugs here cause silent data corruption that accumulates over time and is difficult to diagnose or recover from. Unlike UI bugs (visible immediately), data corruption in stats stores can go unnoticed for weeks and poison decision-making (model selection, item prioritization).

Additional low-coverage persistence code:
- beads_management.py (12.4% - 137 stmts)
- beads_query.py (17.1% - 82 stmts)

Recommended fix:
1. Add unit tests for read/write round-trips on stats stores using temp directories
2. Test edge cases: concurrent writes, corrupted JSON, missing files, disk full
3. Target 70%+ coverage on all *_store.py files
close_reason: Completed coverage improvements

title: restore_beads_stash() drops stash on pop failure, permanently losing .beads/ changes
description:
Problem:
`restore_beads_stash()` in git_helpers.py (lines 38-66) handles stash pop failures by dropping the stash entry entirely. When `git stash pop --index` fails (e.g., due to conflicts between stashed .beads/ changes and newly-pulled changes), the code at line 54 runs `git stash drop`, permanently destroying the stashed data.

Context:
This function is called from `execute_merge_sequence()` in git_operations.py (lines 308, 313). During merges, the beads daemon may modify `.beads/issues.jsonl` concurrently. The merge sequence stashes these changes before `git pull --rebase`, then restores them after. If the pop fails (conflict between daemon's local changes and remote changes to `.beads/`), the stash is silently dropped.

Impact:
- Local .beads/ state (issue assignments, status updates) accumulated since the last sync is permanently lost
- While `bd sync` eventually reconciles state, there is a window where the local beads database is inconsistent with recent operations
- In high-throughput parallel mode, multiple agents may be updating .beads/ concurrently, increasing the probability of this conflict
- The user is told to 'inspect .beads/ changes manually' but the stash is already dropped — there is nothing left to inspect

Fix:
Instead of dropping the stash, preserve it. Options:
1. Log the stash ref (`git stash list`) so users know which stash entry to recover
2. Use `git checkout stash -- .beads/` to force-apply stashed beads changes (theirs-wins strategy, since local beads state is authoritative)
3. At minimum, do NOT drop the stash — leave it in the stash list for manual recovery

Estimated effort: ~30 minutes.

title: Logging infrastructure overhaul: three-channel inconsistency
description:
The codebase has three independent, non-integrated output channels running simultaneously:

1. print() - used in ~15 modules, stdout only, never written to disk
2. logging.getLogger(__name__) - set up in 31 modules but NO handler is configured anywhere, so every logger.debug/info/warning/error call is silently dropped
3. RunLogger/ItemLogger (logging_utils.py) - custom file-based logger used only by orchestrator, maintenance_scheduler, parallel, copilot_sdk

This means critical operational events (race conditions, claim failures, sync warnings) are either silently dropped or only visible on the terminal with no persistence. Five sub-tasks are tracked as children.

Acceptance: single logging hierarchy, two audiences (debug file + warning-level console), no silently dropped messages, no dual print+logger writes for the same event.

title: Unguarded _parse_beads_json callers can crash agents on malformed beads output
description:
## Problem

`_parse_beads_json()` in `src/pokepoke/beads/beads_query.py:159` calls `json.loads()` which can raise `JSONDecodeError` when beads CLI returns output that looks like JSON (starts with `[` or `{`) but is malformed. The function itself does NOT catch this exception — it relies on callers to handle it.

**Some callers properly catch JSONDecodeError:**
- `beads_query.py:201` — catches `(json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError)`
- `beads_management.py:77,130` — catches `(CalledProcessError, json.JSONDecodeError)`
- `beads_metadata.py:29,62,80` — catches `(CalledProcessError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError, TypeError)`

**These callers do NOT catch JSONDecodeError:**
- `decomposition_agent.py:178` — `_create_child_item()` catches only `TimeoutExpired` and `CalledProcessError`
- `decomposition_agent.py:199` — `_update_parent_metadata()` has no exception handler around the call
- `model_sync_beads.py:77` — `_list_existing_model_items()` has no exception handler

## Impact

When beads CLI returns malformed JSON (e.g., truncated output from timeout, mixed warning text with partial JSON), unguarded callers crash with an unhandled `JSONDecodeError`. In the decomposition agent, this means:
- The parent item metadata update fails silently (child items created but parent not updated)
- The decomposition agent crashes, leaving work items in inconsistent state

## Fix

Either:
1. **Preferred**: Make `_parse_beads_json` internally safe — wrap `json.loads()` in try/except and return `None` on `JSONDecodeError` (consistent with its existing None-return for missing JSON)
2. **Alternative**: Add `json.JSONDecodeError` to the except clauses in the 3 unguarded call sites

Option 1 is preferred because it fixes all current AND future callers with a single change and matches the function's existing contract (returns `None` when parsing fails).

title: No cycle detection in beads hierarchy resolution - orchestrator can loop on circular dependencies
description:
## Problem

`resolve_to_leaf_task()` in `beads_hierarchy.py` recursively resolves epics/features to leaf tasks but has no cycle detection. While a `_MAX_DEPTH = 10` guard exists, it only caps recursion depth — it does NOT prevent traversing the same nodes repeatedly within that depth.

Ironically, `_has_unmet_blocking_in_chain()` (line 304-336 in the same file) correctly implements cycle detection with a `_visited` set, proving the pattern is known but wasn't applied to the main resolution path.

## Key Code Location

- `src/pokepoke/beads/beads_hierarchy.py` lines 196-257: `resolve_to_leaf_task()`
- Line 227: `_get_available_children(item.id)` fetches children without tracking visited nodes
- Line 242-252: Recursive call on each child — no visited set passed through

## Scenario

If beads DB contains: Item A (epic) -> Item B (feature) -> Item C (task) -> Item A (circular dep):

1. `resolve_to_leaf_task(A)` calls `_get_available_children(A)` -> finds B
2. `resolve_to_leaf_task(B)` calls `_get_available_children(B)` -> finds C
3. `resolve_to_leaf_task(C)` calls `_get_available_children(C)` -> finds A
4. `resolve_to_leaf_task(A)` again — cycle repeats until depth 10

Each level triggers beads CLI calls (`bd show`, `bd deps`), so a cycle causes ~30 subprocess invocations before the depth guard fires.

## Impact

- **Performance degradation**: ~30 unnecessary beads CLI calls per cycle encounter
- **Cascading slowdown**: If multiple items have circular deps, orchestrator becomes sluggish
- **Silent failure**: Returns `None` after depth exhaustion with no warning about the cycle

## Recommended Fix

1. Add a `_visited: set[str]` parameter to `resolve_to_leaf_task()` (same pattern as `_has_unmet_blocking_in_chain`)
2. Check `if item.id in _visited: return None` with a warning log
3. Pass `_visited | {item.id}` to recursive calls
4. Log a warning when a cycle is detected so operators can fix the beads data
close_reason: Added cycle detection with _visited set to resolve_to_leaf_task(). Cycles are now detected immediately with a warning log instead of wasting ~30 subprocess calls.

title: Rebase timeout leaves worktree in broken state (no abort on TimeoutExpired)
description:
In merge_queue.py _rebase_worktree() (line 275-277), when a git rebase command times out via subprocess.TimeoutExpired, the function returns False WITHOUT attempting to abort the in-progress rebase. This leaves the worktree in a partial rebase state. Subsequent operations (merge, cleanup, retry) on that worktree will fail or produce corrupt results because git thinks a rebase is still in progress.

**Contrast with CalledProcessError path (line 258-273):** That handler correctly runs git rebase --abort before returning False. The TimeoutExpired path is missing the same cleanup.

**Fix:** Add git rebase --abort to the TimeoutExpired handler, matching the CalledProcessError handler pattern:

\\\python
except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
    logger.warning('Rebase timed out in %s', worktree_path)
    try:
        subprocess.run(
            ['git', 'rebase', '--abort'],
            cwd=str(worktree_path),
            capture_output=True, text=True, encoding='utf-8', timeout=30,
        )
    except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
        pass
    return False
\\\

**Impact:** Worktrees stuck in partial rebase state cause cascading merge failures and require manual intervention.
close_reason: Fixed in commit befbb1f

title: Code Review: high-conflict deferral starves normal work
description:
**Problem**
src/pokepoke/parallel_support.py now defers high-conflict items inside _should_skip_item() (lines 118-145) whenever there is another active future or something was dispatched earlier in the cycle.  When slots equals 1 (the common case while another item is running) select_multiple_items() only returns the top candidate.  If that candidate is high-conflict, _should_skip_item() returns True, made_progress stays False, and the while dispatched < slots loop breaks at lines 242-245 without ever considering the lower-priority non-conflict items in eady_items.

Because the ID is never added to  ailed_claim_ids, the next dispatch cycle picks the same high-conflict item again and immediately exits.  The pool sits idle until every other agent finishes, even though there was safe work ready to run.

**Repro**
1. Run the parallel orchestrator with max_parallel_agents >= 2 so two slots exist, and let one normal item keep a worker busy (len(futures) > 0).
2. Ensure eady_items contains a high-conflict-labeled work item followed by a normal item.
3. Call dispatch_items(..., slots=1, ...).  The high-conflict candidate is skipped, the loop breaks, and the normal item never dispatches.  Every subsequent loop repeats the same skip until the active worker finishes.

**Impact**
Throughput stalls whenever a deferred high-conflict item sits at the front of the queue: the dispatcher refuses to start any other work even though capacity exists, so the orchestrator can sit idle for minutes.

**Suggested fix**
Treat deferrals as temporary skips for the rest of the dispatch cycle (e.g., add the ID to the cycle_skip set and continue looping) or otherwise keep searching when an iteration makes no progress, instead of breaking and re-selecting the same item on the next tick.
close_reason: Fixed: dispatch loop now continues past deferred high-conflict items instead of breaking

title: workflow.py bypasses WorkItemSession RAII pattern, defeating crash recovery
description:
**File:** src/pokepoke/orchestration/workflow.py lines 109-120

**Bug:** process_work_item() creates a WorkItemSession but does NOT use it as a context manager. Instead it manually sets private flags (_assigned, _worktree_created, _branch_created) after separate resource acquisition calls. WorkItemSession.__enter__ was designed to: (1) write journal entries at each phase (ASSIGNING -> CREATING_WT -> ACTIVE), (2) provide atomic rollback on failure, (3) enable SessionReconciler crash cleanup. By bypassing __enter__, NO journal is written. If PokePoke crashes between _assign() succeeding (line 105) and _session._assigned = True (line 110), the item stays permanently assigned. If it crashes during setup_worktree(), worktrees are orphaned with no tracking journal.

**Impact (HIGH):** Crash recovery for the primary work item processing path is non-functional. Items can get permanently stuck in assigned state, worktrees can leak, and the SessionReconciler infrastructure provides a false sense of safety.

**Fix:** Refactor process_work_item to use WorkItemSession as a proper context manager, or create a variant of __enter__ that accepts beads_client and lock_timeout. Align the main workflow with the crash-recovery design.

title: reconciliation.py silently swallows path resolution errors, causing orphaned worktrees
description:
Problem:
is_worktree_cleaned() at reconciliation.py:86-91 uses a bare except Exception: continue when resolving worktree paths:

    for wt in active:
        ...
        if path_str:
            try:
                if Path(path_str).resolve() == expected_path:
                    return False
            except Exception:
                continue  # <-- silently skips ALL errors

If Path(path_str).resolve() raises (e.g., PermissionError on a locked directory, OSError on a path exceeding MAX_PATH on Windows, or ValueError on a malformed path), the function silently skips that worktree entry and continues. This means:
1. A worktree that IS still present can be reported as 'cleaned' because the path check was skipped
2. reconcile_completed_item() (line 96) then proceeds to clean up the branch and beads state without actually removing the worktree directory
3. The orphaned worktree directory remains on disk with no tracking entry

On Windows with long worktree paths (the task-{sanitized_id} pattern can produce paths near MAX_PATH), OSError from resolve() is a realistic failure mode.

Fix:
1. Catch only OSError (the realistic failure case), not Exception
2. Log the error at WARNING level so operators can see which paths fail
3. When a path resolution fails, conservatively return False (assume NOT cleaned) rather than skipping

Example fix:
    except OSError as e:
        logger.warning('Failed to resolve worktree path %s: %s', path_str, e)
        return False  # Conservatively assume worktree still exists

Estimated effort: ~15 minutes.

title: Replace os.chdir() with subprocess cwd parameter for agent isolation
description: CRITICAL BLOCKER for parallel agents. Currently workflow.py and agent_runner.py use os.chdir() to switch into worktree directories before invoking Copilot. os.chdir() is process-global - changing CWD in one thread affects ALL threads. This makes it impossible to run two agents concurrently in different worktrees. title: Singleton guard for maintenance agents in parallel mode
description: Maintenance agents (beta_tester, janitor, backlog_cleanup, worktree_cleanup) must not run multiple instances simultaneously - they either modify shared state (janitor cleans worktrees) or produce duplicate work (beta_tester files same issues twice). In the current sequential model this is impossible, but with parallel agents, the orchestrator might trigger maintenance from multiple completing agents at once. Design: (1) Create a MaintenanceScheduler class that owns maintenance scheduling. It replaces the current inline counter checks in orchestrator.py _run_periodic_maintenance(). (2) Use a dict of threading.Lock per agent type (or try_lock from coordination.py). (3) When an agent completes and maintenance is due, MaintenanceScheduler.maybe_run(agent_type) acquires the lock. If already held, skip with a log message. (4) Track run counts atomically with threading-safe counters. (5) Tech Debt and Code Review (beads-only, no worktree, no merging) CAN run in parallel and don't need the guard. Key files: orchestrator.py (_run_periodic_maintenance), agent_runner.py (run_maintenance_agent). Extends PokePoke-lwi2 (file-based singleton lock) with in-process coordination.

title: Gate agent SDK crash displayed as code rejection
description:
When the gate agent crashes due to an infrastructure error (e.g. SDK exception: [Errno 22] Invalid argument), the UI displays it identically to a legitimate code quality rejection. Both show the same red X and the same 'Gate Agent rejected fix:' prefix, making it impossible to distinguish between:

1. The gate agent CRASHED before it could review anything (SDK exception, network error, etc.)
2. The gate agent successfully REVIEWED the code and found it lacking

In the PokePoke-bajj example, two messages are shown back-to-back:
- 'Gate Agent rejected fix: Gate Agent execution failed: SDK exception: [Errno 22] Invalid argument'
- 'Gate Agent rejected fix: Implementation incomplete - RepoWorkerPool created but not integrated into parallel executor'

The first is an infra failure that should NOT trigger a retry with feedback (the gate never even ran). The second is a real rejection that correctly triggered a retry.

Issues:
1. 'Gate Agent rejected fix:' prefix is misleading for SDK crashes - the gate didn't reject anything, it crashed
2. The word 'fix' in 'rejected fix' doesn't make sense for feature items
3. SDK/infra crashes should be visually distinct (e.g. yellow warning vs red rejection)
4. SDK crashes should probably retry the gate agent itself rather than restarting the work agent with corrective feedback based on a crash message
5. The 'Restarting Work Agent with feedback' action after an SDK crash sends meaningless feedback to the work agent since no actual code review occurred
close_reason: Gate agent now returns crashed flag. workflow.py uses inner retry loop (up to 3 attempts) for SDK crashes instead of restarting work agent. Distinct UI messages: warnings for crashes vs rejections for code quality.

title: 62% session failure rate in run 20260305 - agents restart from scratch on each retry
description: In run 20260305_122045_a7e313f7: 8 of 13 items failed (62% failure rate). Each failure consumed all 3 retry attempts (12-19 minutes each), totaling 36-57 minutes of compute per failed item. Key pattern: on each retry, the agent starts a completely new SDK session and re-explores the codebase from scratch. All previous context, progress, and partial work is lost. For example, worker-1 (PokePoke-mjpr) created work_item_session.py and refactored workflow.py in attempt 1, then re-did the exact same exploration and implementation in attempts 2 and 3, failing each time on test fixture incompatibilities it could not resolve. Each retry is essentially identical work rather than building on previous progress. Potential improvements: (1) Pass accumulated context from failed attempt to retry prompt (diff of changes made, test output, etc). (2) Consider checkpointing worktree state between attempts so retries can resume from partial progress. (3) Track failure patterns per work-item type to detect systemic issues early.
close_reason: Core issues addressed: session resume (PokePoke-1i5m/bf65001), retry feedback via prompt templates (ec2d1bc), gate feedback accumulation (4010abe). Agents no longer restart from scratch on retry.

The issue is that each retry creates a brand-new Copilot SDK session via invoke_copilot(), which has zero memory of the previous session. The agent starts fresh with no context about what files were already created/modified, what tests were run, or what errors were encountered. The feedback passed to the retry prompt is just the error string, not a diff or summary of progress. The worktree on disk has the previous attempt's changes, but the agent re-explores and often redoes identical work or makes conflicting edits on top.

title: commit_all_changes uses git add -A in main repo context - stages untracked files
description:
commit_all_changes() in git_operations.py (line 69) uses git add -A which stages ALL files including untracked files. This function is called from the main repo context in:

- cleanup_agents.py:69 - cleanup agent commits in main repo
- worktree_helpers.py:96 - commits pending changes before merge in main repo

This is the same class of bug that was fixed in PokePoke-k65r (P0: preflight repair_git_status discards uncommitted changes). That fix changed preflight_repair.py to use git add -u (tracked files only). But commit_all_changes() was not updated and is still called from main repo paths.

Risk: git add -A in the main repo stages all untracked files, which could include .env files, secret keys, temp debug files, or any file not covered by .gitignore. Pre-commit hooks provide some protection, but they run AFTER staging.

Fix: Add a tracked_only parameter (defaulting to False for backward compat in worktree contexts), or split into commit_all_changes (for worktrees) and commit_tracked_changes (for main repo). Callers in cleanup_agents.py and worktree_helpers.py should use git add -u when operating on the main repo.

Files: src/pokepoke/git_operations.py (line 69), src/pokepoke/cleanup_agents.py (line 69), src/pokepoke/worktree_helpers.py (line 96)
Related: PokePoke-k65r (closed - fixed same pattern in preflight_repair.py)
close_reason: Closed

title: Resource leak: Start-Job processes orphaned when pre-commit hook errors during job processing
description: pre-commit.ps1 spawns 5 Start-Job child processes for static checks (lines 125-147) but the job-processing loop (lines 186-222) has no try/finally block. With ErrorActionPreference=Stop, any unhandled error during Wait-Job/Receive-Job terminates the script and leaves remaining jobs as orphaned pwsh processes. On Windows, child processes are NOT auto-killed when the parent exits, so each leak is a full pwsh process (~50-100MB). Leak paths: (1) exception in Receive-Job for job N leaves jobs N+1..5 running, (2) exception during Start-Job loop leaves already-started jobs, (3) Ctrl+C during processing leaves unprocessed jobs. The build-failure path (lines 178-181) correctly cleans up all jobs, but the normal processing path lacks equivalent protection. Fix: wrap lines 186-222 in try/finally that calls Stop-Job + Remove-Job on all staticJobs in the finally block.
close_reason: Fixed in commit af1861f. Wrapped job processing loop in try/finally and Start-Job creation in try/catch to prevent orphaned pwsh processes.

title: Gate agent loops when work item is already completed or unnecessary
description: When a work item has already been completed on the main branch (e.g., the fix was merged via another branch or the issue no longer applies), the gate agent enters an infinite retry loop. The work agent correctly reports there's nothing to do, but the gate agent rejects it because it doesn't see new commits or changes, triggering another retry cycle. This wastes tokens and blocks the orchestrator. The gate agent prompt needs to be updated to: (1) Check if the work described in the beads item has already been completed on the main/dev branch before rejecting. (2) Compare the current state of the codebase against what the work item asks for - if the fix/feature already exists, approve and close the item. (3) Distinguish between 'agent failed to do the work' vs 'work was already done and no changes are needed'. (4) If the item is genuinely no longer needed (stale, duplicate, or already fixed), the gate agent should approve with a note that the item should be closed as already-resolved rather than forcing another retry. Current behavior: gate rejects -> retry -> agent says nothing to do -> gate rejects -> infinite loop. Expected behavior: gate checks main branch, confirms work is already done, approves/closes the item.
close_reason: Fixed: Gate agent now checks if work already exists on main/dev branch FIRST before rejecting. Supports 'work_already_complete', 'new_work_verified', and 'no_longer_needed' reasons. This prevents infinite retry loops when work was completed via another branch or is no longer applicable.

title: Critical test coverage gap: core pipeline modules at 9-17% coverage
description:
## Problem

Overall test coverage is 35%, but the most safety-critical modules have dangerously low coverage:

- **workflow.py: 10%** (274 stmts, 247 untested) — main work item processing pipeline
- **worktrees.py: 9%** (237 stmts, 215 untested) — worktree lifecycle management
- **worktree_cleanup.py: 13%** (252 stmts, 218 untested) — filesystem cleanup with security invariants
- **git_operations.py: 14%** (185 stmts, 160 untested) — commit, merge, stash operations
- **beads_management.py: 14%** (160 stmts, 137 untested) — item claiming, assignment, TOCTOU protection
- **agent_runner.py: 15%** (175 stmts, 148 untested) — agent execution and lifecycle
- **work_item_session.py: 17%** (122 stmts, 101 untested) — RAII resource acquisition/rollback
- **copilot_sdk.py: 19%** (184 stmts, 149 untested) — AI backend invocation

## Impact

The pre-commit hook enforces 80% on *modified files*, which creates a false sense of security. The vast majority of the core pipeline — resource lifecycle, cleanup, error recovery, and data integrity paths — is untested. Regressions in these paths would go completely undetected.

Particularly dangerous untested paths:
1. **Failure/rollback paths** in work_item_session.py and workflow.py — the code that runs when things go wrong is the least tested
2. **Worktree cleanup on Windows** — symlink/junction detection, permission handling, retry logic (13% covered)
3. **Beads TOCTOU claiming** — the locking and atomicity code in beads_management.py (14% covered)
4. **Git merge conflict handling** — merge_conflict.py at 14%

## Recommended approach

Prioritize coverage by risk:
1. work_item_session.py — RAII rollback paths (most critical for resource leaks)
2. worktree_cleanup.py — security-sensitive filesystem operations
3. beads_management.py — data integrity (claiming, assignment)
4. workflow.py — main processing pipeline error paths
5. git_operations.py — merge and commit failure scenarios

Target: raise each critical module to >=60% as a first milestone, then 80%.

title: Merge sequence has no rollback — failed merges/pushes leave main repo in broken state
description:
execute_merge_sequence() and merge_worktree() perform checkout->stash->pull->merge->push but have NO rollback on any failure path. This leaves the main repo in a broken state for all subsequent agents.

Three concrete failure scenarios:

1. **Merge conflict — no git merge --abort**: When git merge --no-ff fails at git_operations.py:316-329, the function returns (False, error, unmerged_files) but the repo is left in a merge-conflict state (MERGE_HEAD present). Subsequent agents trying to merge other worktrees will fail because the main repo is in a conflicted state.

2. **Pull rebase failure — no git rebase --abort**: When git pull --rebase fails at git_operations.py:301-309, the function returns but the repo may be in a rebase-in-progress state (REBASE_HEAD present). The stash is restored, but the broken rebase state persists.

3. **Push failure — no git reset --hard HEAD~1**: When git push fails at worktrees.py:254-259, the local merge commit stays in the main branch. The remote doesn't have this commit. The next agent's git pull --rebase will attempt to rebase on diverged history, causing cascading merge failures or silent history rewriting.

CONFIRMED: git merge --abort, git rebase --abort, and git reset --hard appear NOWHERE in any Python source file — only in markdown prompt templates that instruct agents (not the orchestrator itself).

This is a primary contributor to cascading merge failures under parallel agent execution. Each failed merge poisons the main repo state for all subsequent merge attempts.

Fix: Add rollback to each failure path:
- On merge failure: git merge --abort before returning
- On rebase failure: git rebase --abort before returning
- On push failure: git reset --hard HEAD~1 before returning
- On validate_post_merge exception: catch and rollback (line 331-347 uses check=True with no try/except)

title: Core pipeline modules at 10-13% test coverage - critical reliability risk
description:
Problem: The core business-logic pipeline of PokePoke has dangerously low test coverage. These modules form the critical path (claim item -> create worktree -> process work -> gate validate -> merge) but have almost no automated safety net.

Evidence from coverage.json (overall: 27.6%):

Zero coverage (0%) on significant modules:
- models/model_sync.py (218 stmts) - model discovery/synchronization
- git/repo_worker_pool.py (135 stmts) - multi-repo worker scheduling
- stats/session_reconciler.py (107 stmts) - session stats reconciliation
- models/model_sync_parsing.py (91 stmts) - model sync response parsing
- git/repo_config_loader.py (78 stmts) - per-repo configuration loading
- git/repo_picker.py (74 stmts) - repository selection logic

Critical-path modules at 10-13% coverage:
- orchestration/workflow.py (253 stmts, 10.7%) - THE main work item processing pipeline
- agents/parallel_support.py (257 stmts, 9.3%) - parallel agent scheduling infrastructure
- worktrees/worktrees.py (207 stmts, 10.6%) - worktree creation and lifecycle
- git/git_operations.py (185 stmts, 13.5%) - high-level git merge/rebase workflows
- beads/beads_management.py (183 stmts, 12.6%) - item claiming and assignment
- worktrees/worktree_merge_handler.py (114 stmts, 11.4%) - merge sequencing in worktrees
- agents/cleanup_agents.py (193 stmts, 11.9%) - post-work cleanup agent execution

Why this matters:
- workflow.py is the heart of the orchestrator. Every work item flows through it. At 10.7% coverage, regressions in retry logic, gate invocation, or timeout handling go undetected.
- beads_management.py handles the critical double-claim prevention logic. At 12.6%, the TOCTOU-safe claim-verify-sync sequence has minimal test coverage.
- worktrees.py manages isolation boundaries. At 10.6%, worktree leaks or stale cleanup bugs won't be caught.
- The 80% gate only applies to MODIFIED files. These modules haven't been modified recently, so they bypass the coverage gate entirely.

Note: This is distinct from PokePoke-t3gf (module splitting for maintainability) and PokePoke-x4tf (contract testing). This issue is specifically about the reliability risk from untested critical-path code.

Acceptance criteria:
- workflow.py, beads_management.py, worktrees.py each reach 50%+ line coverage
- At least one test per public function in model_sync.py and repo_worker_pool.py
- parallel_support.py reaches 30%+ coverage (currently 9.3%)
- Tests cover the happy path AND at least one error/edge case per critical function
- No regressions in existing tests

title: PokePoke process keeps running after UI is exited, causing mischief
description: When the PokePoke desktop UI is closed/exited, the backend orchestrator process continues running in the background. This orphaned process continues performing autonomous operations (claiming work items, creating worktrees, invoking Copilot CLI, making commits) without user oversight. This is dangerous because: (1) The user believes operations have stopped but they haven't. (2) Autonomous agents may make unwanted changes to the repo. (3) Resources (CPU, network, API calls) are consumed unnecessarily. (4) Multiple orphaned processes can accumulate across sessions. title: SIGINT handler calls sys.exit(), bypassing session finalization
description:
## Summary

The signal handler in `signal_handlers.py` (line 104) calls `sys.exit(exit_code)` after `request_shutdown()`. This raises `SystemExit` (a `BaseException` subclass), which is NOT caught by the orchestrator's `except KeyboardInterrupt` or `except Exception` blocks. As a result, `_finalize_session()` is never called on Ctrl+C.

## Root Cause

`signal_handlers.py:104`: `sys.exit(exit_code)`

The custom SIGINT handler replaces Python's default handler (which raises `KeyboardInterrupt`). The custom handler raises `SystemExit` instead, which bypasses both exception handlers in the orchestrator main loop:
- `except KeyboardInterrupt` (line 306) - does NOT catch `SystemExit`
- `except Exception` (line 315) - does NOT catch `SystemExit` (it's `BaseException`)

The `finally` block runs but only stops the UI and merge queue - it does not call `_finalize_session()`.

## Impact

- Every Ctrl+C produces an incomplete run log (no final stats, no session summary)
- `RunLogger` is not properly finalized/flushed
- The `except KeyboardInterrupt` block at line 306 is effectively dead code
- Session stats are lost

## Fix

Remove `sys.exit(exit_code)` from the signal handler. Let the handler only call `request_shutdown()` and return. The main loop's `is_shutting_down()` check will exit cleanly, and the shutdown watchdog in `shutdown.py` already handles force-exit as a fallback for truly hung processes.
close_reason: Closed

title: Race condition: orchestrator writes to shared failed_claim_ids set without lock in parallel mode
description:
In orchestrator.py, _OrchestratorContext.failed_claim_ids is a plain set[str] (line 127) shared between the main orchestrator thread and ThreadPoolExecutor worker threads in parallel mode (line 390 passes the same object to run_parallel_loop).

The parallel_worker_pool._update_failed_ids() function (lines 124-138) correctly acquires a lock when updating from worker threads. However, the orchestrator's own _run_main_loop() writes to the SAME set WITHOUT any lock:
- Line 327: ctx.failed_claim_ids.add(selected_item.id) — unprotected
- Line 330: ctx.failed_claim_ids.clear() — unprotected
- Line 328: len(ctx.failed_claim_ids) — unprotected read

While CPython's GIL makes individual set.add() atomic, set.clear() racing with set.add() from another thread can cause RuntimeError (set changed size during iteration) if any thread iterates the set, and len() during mutation can return stale values. More importantly, the .clear() on line 330 (on success) can discard items just added by parallel workers, causing items to be re-attempted instead of skipped.

Impact: In parallel mode (--max-agents > 1), workers and orchestrator can lose failed-claim tracking, causing (a) repeated attempts on permanently failing items, (b) potential RuntimeError crashes from concurrent set mutation during iteration.

Fix: Either (a) wrap all failed_claim_ids access in orchestrator.py with the same lock used by _update_failed_ids, (b) make failed_claim_ids a thread-safe wrapper class with internal lock, or (c) replace .clear() with per-item .discard() to avoid wiping worker state.

Location: src/pokepoke/orchestration/orchestrator.py lines 127, 297, 327-330, 390

title: abort_merge() return value ignored on failure paths in worktree_finalization.py
description:
In worktree_finalization.py merge_worktree_to_dev(), two failure paths call abort_merge() but discard its return value. If abort fails, the repository is left in a MERGING state, blocking all subsequent merge operations until manual intervention.

Bug location: Lines 168-169 and 174-176

Inconsistency: The same function correctly checks abort_merge() return on lines 155-157:
  abort_success, abort_error = abort_merge()
  if not abort_success:
      return False

But on lines 168-169 and 174-176:
  if is_merge_in_progress():
      abort_merge()  # Return value DISCARDED
  return False

Impact: When abort_merge() fails (filesystem issues, git lock contention, timeout), the main repository remains in a MERGING state. All future merge_worktree_to_dev() calls fail at check_main_repo_ready_for_merge(). Requires manual git merge --abort to recover.

Fix: Check the abort return value and log the failure, matching the pattern at lines 155-157.

title: Code Review: backend concurrency test is sequential
description:
## Problem
	ests/integration/test_e2e_autonomous_backends.py::test_concurrent_backend_operations claims to validate concurrent backend switching but the implementation is purely sequential. It simply calls set_active_backend() and get_active_backend() in order with no threads, async tasks, or contention. The docstring and inline comment promise a race-condition test, yet no concurrency primitive is used.

## Impact
Because the test never exercises simultaneous backend operations, it will happily pass even if the global backend state were to break under real concurrent access. This gives a false sense of safety and could allow regressions in the shared backend registry.

## Recommendation
Either rename/scope the test to reflect that it only verifies sequential switching, OR (preferred) make it truly concurrent: spin up multiple threads/tasks that rapidly switch backends and assert the active backend and sync strategy remain consistent. Use threading.Thread or concurrent.futures to surface the intended race conditions.

title: Atomic work item claiming to prevent parallel thread races
description: With multiple agent threads selecting work items simultaneously, there is a TOCTOU race in the current claiming flow: Thread A calls bd ready, sees item X is available. Thread B also calls bd ready, also sees item X. Both call assign_and_sync_item() for X - one succeeds, one wastes a worktree creation. Current mitigation: assign_and_sync_item() in beads_management.py checks the assignee field before assigning, but two threads could pass that check simultaneously. Fix: (1) Use acquire_lock('claim') from coordination.py around the entire select-and-claim sequence. (2) Better: maintain an in-process set of claimed_item_ids (protected by a threading.Lock) that threads check before attempting to claim. Thread adds item ID to the set atomically, then calls bd update --assign. If bd update fails, remove from set. (3) The select_work_item() function in work_item_selection.py should accept a claimed_ids set parameter and filter those out of the ready list before presenting options. This is complementary to PokePoke-n5yu (file-based claim lock for cross-process) but handles the in-process multi-thread case more efficiently. Key files: work_item_selection.py, beads_management.py (assign_and_sync_item), workflow.py (process_work_item).

title: Decompose process_work_item God Function in workflow.py (340+ lines, 15+ state vars)
description:
## Problem

`process_work_item()` in `src/pokepoke/orchestration/workflow.py` (lines 45-400) is a 340+ line function that manages at least 6 distinct responsibilities in a single scope:

1. **Timeout tracking** — elapsed time, restart counting, remaining timeout calculation
2. **Model selection & prompt building** — model assignment, template selection, resume vs. fresh prompts
3. **Copilot invocation** — backend call, result parsing, crash/timeout detection
4. **Cleanup orchestration** — cleanup agent dispatch with timeout protection
5. **Gate agent execution** — nested retry loop with separate crash/timeout counters and resume session management
6. **Result finalization** — decomposition triggers, beads comments, stats recording

The function uses 15+ local state variables (`timeout_restart_count`, `copilot_failure_count`, `gate_rejection_count`, `resume_session_id`, `resume_output_summary`, `process_crashed_this_session`, `last_retry_was_gate_feedback`, `accumulated_feedback`, `gate_crash_attempts`, `gate_timeout_attempts`, etc.) that form an implicit state machine with non-obvious transitions.

## Impact

- **Reliability risk**: Modifying gate retry logic risks breaking timeout handling and vice versa — the interleaved state makes it nearly impossible to reason about one concern independently.
- **Testability**: Individual phases cannot be unit tested in isolation. Integration tests must exercise the entire 340-line flow.
- **Cognitive load**: Any contributor must hold all 6 responsibilities in mind simultaneously to make safe changes. The `# noqa: C901` on line 45 acknowledges the complexity but doesn't address it.

## Recommended Approach

Extract Method pattern (Martin Fowler) — decompose into a state-machine driver + phase handlers:

- `_run_work_agent_phase()` — prompt building, copilot invocation, crash/timeout retry
- `_run_cleanup_phase()` — cleanup agent dispatch
- `_run_gate_agent_phase()` — gate execution with crash/timeout retry loops
- `_handle_gate_rejection()` — rejection counting, feedback accumulation, decomposition trigger
- `WorkItemProcessingState` dataclass to replace the 15+ loose local variables

Each phase returns a typed result that the driver interprets, eliminating the implicit state transitions.

title: Fix DEP0190 deprecation warning in child process spawning
description:
Node.js is showing a deprecation warning when spawning child processes with shell=true and passing args array. This can lead to security vulnerabilities as arguments are not escaped, only concatenated.

Warning message:
(node:29468) [DEP0190] DeprecationWarning: Passing args to a child process with shell option true can lead to security vulnerabilities, as the arguments are not escaped, only concatenated.

Affected code:
- src/beads.ts: spawn('bd', ['ready', '--json'], { shell: true })
- src/copilot.ts: spawn('copilot', ['-p', prompt, '--allow-all-tools', '--no-color'], { shell: true })

Solution:
Either remove shell:true and handle command construction properly, or switch to using a single command string without the args array when shell is needed.
