title: P0: preflight repair_git_status discards uncommitted changes - work is lost
description: repair_git_status() in preflight_repair.py silently destroys uncommitted work. The function first runs 'git add -A' which stages ALL files indiscriminately, then attempts 'git commit'. If the commit fails (e.g. pre-commit hooks reject it), it falls back to 'git stash push -m pokepoke-preflight-stash'. The stash is NEVER popped back anywhere in the codebase - there is no corresponding 'git stash pop' or 'git stash apply' for the preflight stash. This means the user's uncommitted work is silently moved into the git stash and effectively lost/hidden. Users lose in-progress work without any warning or recovery mechanism. Additionally, 'git add -A' is dangerous as it stages everything including temporary files and potentially secrets not yet in .gitignore. Fix: (1) NEVER stash or discard uncommitted changes. (2) Instead of stashing, invoke a cleanup agent (Copilot CLI) to fix the failures (test failures, lint errors, etc.) and get the work properly committed. (3) If the cleanup agent fails, invoke another cleanup agent in a retry loop with corrective feedback from the previous failure, repeating until one succeeds and the commit goes through. (4) Replace 'git add -A' with targeted staging. (5) Log clear warnings so users know what is happening. Key file: src/pokepoke/preflight_repair.py lines 22-57
close_reason: Fix merged to master in commit 9a136fd: replaced git add -A and silent stash with targeted staging and cleanup agent retry loop

title: Code Review: Gate chips pull verdicts from other sessions
description:
## Summary
`AgentsPanel` builds a single `childrenByParent` map for **all** agent cards but `renderAgentCard` uses it to show gate summaries inside every session group. Card IDs and agent IDs are reused each session (they only encode the worker name + iteration), so the global map mixes children from different sessions and the gate chip on a card will show verdicts from an unrelated, older run.

## Details
- At the top of `desktop/src/components/AgentsPanel.tsx` lines 91-135, `childrenByParent` is keyed only by `card_id` or `agent_id`, with no session qualifier.
- `renderSessionGroup` later rebuilds a `sessionChildrenByParent` map per session so the tree layout stays local, but `renderAgentCard` (lines 128-140) still calls the global `childrenByParent.get(...)` to find gate children and derive `gateSummary`.
- `_build_card_id()` in `agent_registry.py` returns `f"{agent_id}::v{iteration}"`, and `_worker_counter` resets every orchestrator run, so card IDs collide across sessions. When you start a new session on the same work item, the new root card has the same key as a previous session, so `childrenByParent` returns the old gate agent instead of the current one.

## Impact
- The gate status chip on an "Active" card immediately shows the verdict from the prior session (often "Gate failed") even though the new gate has not run yet.
- Previous sessions can also suddenly show the current session's gate result because the shared key was overwritten.
- Operators cannot trust the gate badge to reflect the current attempt; it may cause them to skip rerunning gates or misinterpret why a retry is still executing.

## Fix
Scope the lookup to the session being rendered. Either pass the per-session `sessionChildrenByParent` map down to `renderAgentCard`, or include `session_id` in the map key (e.g., `${sessionId}:${cardId}`) so cross-session collisions are impossible.

title: Failure-to-success reconciliation path in _finalize_item_result is untested
description:
When a Copilot session reports failure, _finalize_item_result (workflow_helpers.py L324-352) calls reconcile_completed_item() to check if work actually landed. If all three evidence checks pass (beads_closed, commits_on_default, worktree_cleaned), the item is silently upgraded from FAILURE to SUCCESS. This entire code path has zero test coverage:

- reconciliation.py has no test file and is never imported by any test
- TestFinalizeItemResult in test_workflow_coverage.py only tests the success path (result.success=True), never the failure path that triggers reconciliation
- A false-positive bug in reconciliation (incorrectly concluding work landed) would cause items to be marked complete without the work actually being done, with no error or warning

The reconciliation logic itself is conservatively designed (all three independent checks must agree), which mitigates the risk. But untested code is unverified code.

Fix:
1. Add unit tests for reconciliation.py: test is_beads_item_closed, default_branch_has_merge_commit, is_worktree_cleaned, and reconcile_completed_item with mocked subprocess calls
2. Add a test for _finalize_item_result with result.success=False that exercises the reconciliation path (both reconciled=True and reconciled=False branches)
3. Add a test that verifies a false-positive scenario is correctly handled (e.g., worktree cleaned but no merge commit = NOT reconciled)

Key files:
- src/pokepoke/reconciliation.py (0% test coverage)
- src/pokepoke/workflow_helpers.py L324-352 (untested failure path)
- tests/test_workflow_coverage.py L610-674 (only tests success path)

title: Code Review: Worktree branch guard still reuses main
description:
**Files**: src/pokepoke/worktrees/worktrees.py, src/pokepoke/orchestration/workflow.py`n`n**Problem**:
- _check_existing_directory() (around L90-L128) only removes worktrees when git branch --show-current returns a name containing /, 	ask/, or efs/. Default branches like main/master do not match this heuristic, so a directory checked out to main passes validation and is reused even though it is on the wrong branch.
- The new guard in process_work_item() correctly aborts when it sees that worktree on main, but cleanup preserves the directory. On the next loop create_worktree() hits _check_existing_directory() and hands the same main worktree back, so the guard fires again and the item is stuck.
`n**Impact**:
- Worktree isolation is still broken: agents can keep landing work directly on main, or the orchestrator can no longer process the item without manual cleanup.
`n**Suggested fix**:
- In _check_existing_directory() treat *any* non-empty branch that differs from xpected_branch as a fatal mismatch (no slash/prefix heuristics) and force-remove the directory before returning None.
- Consider doing the same in _find_existing_worktree() or immediately after the guard fails so the worktree is rebuilt automatically.

title: Agent subprocess output leaks to parent console instead of agent panel
description: When running PokePoke from a terminal (e.g. python -m pokepoke.orchestrator --autonomous --continuous), output from agent subprocesses (pre-commit hooks, git commits, beads sync) leaks to the parent console instead of being captured and routed to the agent's output panel in the desktop UI. title: Orchestrator crash under high parallelism: merge-queue.lock timeout, git index.lock contention, tasklist spam
description: Running with --max-agents 15 caused cascading failures leading to crash. Three interrelated problems: (1) merge-queue.lock could not be acquired - filelock.Timeout raised in coordination.py acquire_lock() during worktree finalization for PokePoke-b6uv. The lock holder never released it (likely stuck or crashed). (2) git index.lock contention - concurrent git operations from multiple agents created .git/index.lock conflicts. git status --porcelain timed out after 10s and later returned exit code 4294967295 (0xFFFFFFFF). (3) tasklist /FI IMAGENAME eq copilot.exe /FO CSV timed out after 5s on every single poll cycle, flooding the console with hundreds of timeout messages. Under 15 parallel agents the system was overwhelmed. Fixes needed: increase merge lock timeout or add retry with backoff, serialize git operations through a git lock (not just merge lock), and fix tasklist timeout (see PokePoke-tezl).

title: Worktree cleanup retry loop blocks agent thread for up to 78s per stuck worktree
description: In worktree_cleanup.py, force_remove_directory() has a retry loop: _CLEANUP_MAX_RETRIES=5 with wait_for_process_cleanup(max_wait=3.0) + capped exponential backoff (3s, 6s, 12s, 24s, 30s) = ~78s worst case per stuck worktree. This runs on the worker thread which holds a semaphore slot in parallel mode. Windows file locking issues (antivirus, indexing) can cause all retries to fail, and the worktree goes to uncleaned manifest. The 78s of blocking per stuck worktree is wasted agent capacity. Consider: make cleanup fire-and-forget by immediately adding to manifest and letting the maintenance Worktree Cleanup agent handle retries asynchronously, or move cleanup to a dedicated background thread that does not hold a semaphore slot.

title: On pre-commit hook failure during merge, restart work agent on worktree instead of running cleanup on main
description: Currently when pre-commit hooks fail during the merge commit to main (git_operations.py:328), the merge aborts and a cleanup agent is launched to fix issues ON MAIN. This blocks all subsequent merges and maintenance. Better approach: (1) abort the merge (already done), (2) merge master INTO the worktree (reverse direction), (3) restart the work agent on the worktree with feedback about what pre-commit hooks failed, (4) let the agent fix the issues in the isolated worktree, (5) re-submit to merge queue. This keeps main always clean and eliminates the entire dirty-main cleanup cascade. The gate agent could also be enhanced to run pre-commit hooks in read-only mode as part of validation.
close_reason: Implemented pre-commit hook failure recovery: detects hook failures during merge, reverse-merges main into worktree, launches fix agent in worktree CWD, retries merge. 37 tests, 100% coverage on new modules.

title: Remove auto-push (step 13) — pushing should be manual
description: The merge flow currently includes several remote-sync operations that should all be removed together since PokePoke should only perform local merges. Steps to remove: (8) git stash push -- .beads/ — only exists to protect beads files from the rebase in step 9. (8a) the stash conditional check. (9) git pull --rebase origin target — syncs local branch with remote before merge; unnecessary if we are not pushing. (10) Restore .beads/ stash — undoes step 8 after rebase. (13) git push with 3 retries and exponential backoff — auto-pushes to remote. (14) post-push is_worktree_merged diagnostic check — warning-only, no control flow impact. PokePoke should merge to the local target branch and stop. The user decides when to pull/push. This simplifies the merge to: checkout target -> merge --no-ff -> validate -> cleanup. Reasons: (1) user may want to review before pushing, (2) push/pull failures add complexity PokePoke shouldn't own, (3) rollback-on-push-failure is destructive, (4) the beads stash dance is pure accidental complexity from the rebase, (5) removing network ops from the critical path improves reliability. Also removes rebase conflict as a failure mode (git rebase --abort in retry table). Note: is_worktree_merged is still used in startup_cleanup.py — that usage stays.
close_reason: Removed auto-push (step 13), pull --rebase (step 9), beads stash/restore (steps 8/8a/10), and post-push verification (step 14) from merge flow. PokePoke now performs local-only merges: checkout -> merge --no-ff -> validate -> cleanup. Updated step tracker, diagrams, and all tests.

title: Silent stash pop failures in git_operations.py can leave repo dirty
description:
In git_operations.py execute_merge_sequence(), beads daemon changes are stashed before git pull --rebase (lines 314-318). However, both stash pop calls (lines 329 and 337) silently swallow CalledProcessError with bare 'pass' statements. If stash pop fails due to a conflict, the .beads/ changes are lost in the stash and the working directory may be left in an inconsistent state.

The comment on line 339 says 'beads will re-sync anyway' but this assumption is fragile - if the beads daemon is not running, or if the stashed changes included manual edits, data is silently lost. Furthermore, stale stash entries accumulate over time (one per failed pop), causing 'git stash list' pollution and potential confusion.

Fix: (1) Log a warning when stash pop fails so operators can investigate. (2) After a failed pop, attempt 'git stash drop' to prevent stale stash accumulation. (3) Consider using 'git stash pop --index' to preserve both staged and unstaged state. (4) At minimum, print the conflict details so the failure is visible in logs.

Key file: src/pokepoke/git_operations.py, lines 327-339
Severity: Medium-High - silent data loss and stale stash accumulation
close_reason: Handled stash pop failures and added sdk_event_handler coverage

title: Gate-passed items that fail only at merge should retry merge, not re-run work+gate
description: When a work item passes the gate agent but fails during merge (e.g. merge conflicts, dirty master, file length violation at commit), the orchestrator returns WorkItemResult(success=False) and the item goes back to the ready queue. On the next pickup, the entire pipeline runs from scratch: work agent -> cleanup -> gate agent -> merge. This is wasteful because the work is already done, committed in the worktree, and gate-validated. The worktree is even preserved. In the 20260421_132756 run, PokePoke-jixa6 was attempted 8 times — each time redoing work+gate only to fail again at merge. Fix: when finalization detects a merge-only failure (work+gate succeeded but merge failed), mark the item with a 'merge_retry' flag. On re-pickup, if the worktree exists with committed work and the item has merge_retry set, skip directly to the merge step. This requires: (1) A new WorkItemResult field like failure_stage='merge' to distinguish merge failures from work/gate failures. (2) The orchestrator checking for existing worktree+commits on re-pickup. (3) A fast-path in process_work_item that skips work+gate and goes straight to merge when the worktree is already validated.

title: Orphaned worktrees accumulate unchecked during long runs (11 -> 31), never auto-cleaned
description: DECISION: Merged-and-pushed worktrees are safe to ignore/defer — they're not a correctness risk. Only unmerged/uncommitted worktrees need protection. However, if unmerged worktrees are significantly behind master (many commits behind), they should be cleaned up rather than preserved since resuming from them will create more merge conflicts than starting fresh. IMPLEMENTATION: (1) After each agent completes, attempt inline cleanup with git worktree remove + prune (don't wait for maintenance agent window); (2) For merged worktrees that fail to remove (Windows file locks), add to a deferred cleanup list and retry at end-of-run; (3) For unmerged worktrees, check how far behind master they are — if >N commits behind, clean them up; (4) Classify worktrees in pre-flight as merged-uncleaned vs unmerged-stale vs unmerged-active and only warn on the latter two; (5) Keep the maintenance agent as fallback but don't depend on it finding an idle window

title: Uncleanable main repo should be a critical error with retry before halt

This is wrong — if the main repo cannot be made clean, NO further merges can succeed (they all hit the same dirty check), and continuing to spawn work agents produces work that can never be merged. This is an invariant violation. Required changes: (1) Retry the cleanup agent + re-check loop (steps 3b/3c) multiple times (e.g. 3 attempts) before giving up, to avoid halting for transient issues. (2) If all retries fail, stop spawning new work agents immediately. (3) Log a CRITICAL-level alert with the list of dirty files and cleanup agent output. (4) Surface a clear user-facing message explaining the repo needs manual cleanup. (5) Terminate the orchestrator or enter a paused state rather than continuing to burn tokens on work that cannot be merged. With the dedicated merge worktree (PokePoke-hro7e) this entire category goes away since the merge worktree is always clean by construction.

title: execute_merge_sequence missing TimeoutExpired handling - repo left dirty on timeout
description:
**Bug:** git_operations.py:execute_merge_sequence() (lines 276-363) sets explicit timeouts on all three subprocess calls (checkout=30s, pull=120s, merge=60s) but only catches CalledProcessError. If any command hits its timeout, subprocess.TimeoutExpired propagates uncaught, breaking the function's return-type contract (bool, str, list[str]) and skipping all recovery logic.

**Worst case — merge timeout (line 340):** If git merge --no-ff is killed at 60s, MERGE_HEAD can persist in the repo. The merge-abort logic at lines 350-358 is inside the xcept CalledProcessError block and is never reached. The repo is left in a dirty merge-in-progress state.

**Stash loss — pull timeout (line 319):** If git pull --rebase times out after beads changes were stashed (line 314), the stash-restore at line 331-332 is inside the CalledProcessError handler and is skipped. Beads stash is silently lost.

**Irony:** The *abort* commands at line 329 correctly catch (CalledProcessError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired), showing awareness of the pattern — it just wasn't applied to the primary commands.

**Fix:** Add subprocess.TimeoutExpired to each except clause, with appropriate rollback:
- Checkout timeout: return failure tuple
- Pull timeout: abort rebase + restore stash + return failure tuple  
- Merge timeout: abort merge + return failure tuple with unmerged files

**Affected callers:** worktrees.merge_worktree() (line 271) passes the return value directly. A TimeoutExpired exception instead of a tuple will crash the merge handler and any upstream logic that destructures the result.

**Mitigating factor:** WorkItemSession.cleanup_on_failure() provides a safety net by aborting in-progress merges during session cleanup, but only for code paths that go through the session lifecycle. Direct callers of xecute_merge_sequence have no protection.
close_reason: Closed

title: Work item permanently stuck in assigned state when finalize_work_item fails
description:
## Summary

When `finalize_work_item()` returns `False` (merge failure, push rejection, conflict resolution failure), the work item is never unassigned in beads. It remains permanently stuck in `assigned`/`in_progress` state and no agent will ever pick it up again.

## Root Cause

In `workflow.py`, `unassign_item()` is only called on line 120 (worktree setup failure). On the success path when finalization fails (lines 261-310), and on the general failure path (lines 311-341), and in the `finally` block (lines 343-351), `unassign_item()` is never called.

## Impact

- **Critical in continuous/parallel mode**: Every merge failure permanently orphans a work item
- Silently accumulates over multiple sessions with no visibility
- Items become invisible to `bd ready` and can only be recovered by manual `bd update`

## Reproduction

1. Run PokePoke in continuous mode
2. Have a work item whose merge conflicts cannot be auto-resolved
3. Item stays assigned forever after failure

## Fix

Add `unassign_item(item.id)` in two places:
1. In the `finally` block (line 343) when `worktree_path is not None` and the function is exiting with failure
2. In the failure path (line 311-341) before returning the failed result

Track a `was_assigned` boolean set to `True` after `assign_and_sync_item` succeeds, and check it in `finally`.
close_reason: Fixed: unassign work item in finally block when processing fails after assignment

title: Worktree manifest race condition: parallel agents can silently lose entries
description:
## Summary

`add_uncleaned_worktree()` in `worktree_cleanup.py` (lines 150-158) performs a non-atomic read-modify-write on the uncleaned worktrees JSON manifest with no file locking. In parallel mode, concurrent agents failing cleanup simultaneously can overwrite each other's entries, silently losing orphaned worktree records.

## Root Cause

`worktree_cleanup.py:150-158`:
1. `load_worktree_manifest()` reads the JSON file
2. Dict is modified in memory
3. `save_worktree_manifest()` writes back

No file lock protects this sequence. Two agents entering `add_uncleaned_worktree()` concurrently will both read the same manifest, both add their entry, and the last writer wins - the other entry is silently discarded.

The same race exists in `remove_from_manifest()` (lines 161-166).

## Impact

- Orphaned worktree directories are never retried by the cleanup agent
- In parallel sessions with frequent Windows lock errors, the manifest becomes unreliable
- Disk space gradually consumed by untracked worktree directories that accumulate with no cleanup path

## Fix

Wrap `load_worktree_manifest()`/`save_worktree_manifest()` sequences with a file lock. The `coordination.py` module already provides file-locking infrastructure (`worktree_setup_lock`, `merge_lock`) that could be extended or reused for manifest access.
close_reason: Fixed: Added file locking (manifest_lock) to prevent race conditions in worktree manifest operations

title: shutil.rmtree in worktree cleanup follows symlinks - risk of deleting files outside worktree
description:
**Security / Data Integrity Risk**

In worktree_cleanup.py:77, `force_remove_directory()` falls back to `shutil.rmtree(str(dir_path), onerror=_handle_remove_readonly)` when `git worktree remove --force` fails. On Windows (the primary platform for this project), `shutil.rmtree` does NOT use the symlink-resistant implementation (which requires fd-based OS functions unavailable on Windows). This means symbolic links or junctions inside a worktree directory cause `shutil.rmtree` to traverse and delete files *outside* the worktree boundary.

The `_handle_remove_readonly` error handler (line 23-26) exacerbates this by calling `os.chmod(path, stat.S_IWRITE)` on every permission error, actively stripping read-only protection from files it encounters - including files reached via symlink that are outside the worktree.

**Attack vector:** A malicious or adversarial beads work item could instruct the Copilot agent to create a symlink inside the worktree pointing to critical directories (e.g., the main repo's .git, the user's home directory, or other worktrees). When PokePoke cleans up the worktree after completion or failure, `shutil.rmtree` follows the symlink and deletes the target. Since PokePoke runs autonomously, there is no human review step to catch this.

**Remediation:**
1. Add a symlink check before `shutil.rmtree`: reject or skip removal if `dir_path.is_symlink()` is True
2. Add path boundary validation: verify `dir_path.resolve()` is inside the expected worktrees directory before deletion
3. Walk the directory tree manually with `os.walk(topdown=False, followlinks=False)` instead of `shutil.rmtree` to avoid following symlinks
4. Validate no symlinks exist inside the worktree before calling rmtree (scan with `Path.rglob` checking `is_symlink()`)

**Affected code:**
- src/pokepoke/worktrees/worktree_cleanup.py:29 (force_remove_directory)
- src/pokepoke/worktrees/worktree_cleanup.py:23-26 (_handle_remove_readonly)

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `force_remove_directory()` never follows symlinks when deleting worktree contents
- Path boundary validation ensures deletion stays within the worktrees directory
- Test coverage for: symlink inside worktree, junction point, worktree path that is itself a symlink
- Existing worktree cleanup tests still pass

Currently the orchestrator queries bd ready, picks an item, submits it to the thread pool, and only then does the cap check fire inside the worker. Move the cap check to the scheduling phase: query bd ready, filter out items with gate_rejection_count >= cap, then submit only viable items. This also makes the flow cleaner — process_work_item should not contain a bail-out at line 2.
close_reason: Moved gate rejection cap pre-check from workflow entry to orchestrator scheduling (both single-worker and parallel paths). Items at/above cap are now filtered before claiming.

Items at the rejection cap will still be selected, claimed, and processed wastefully in single-worker mode. Fix: either add _exceeds_gate_rejection_cap to _filter_available (preferred — fixes both paths) or add it explicitly to select_work_item. Also, test_items_at_cap_filtered_during_selection is a no-op pass statement and should be replaced with actual test coverage for the select_work_item path.

title: Include agent name in item log file names
